postings.description:
WE ARE

The European External Action Service (EEAS) is the European Union’s diplomatic service. Since 2011, the EEAS carries out the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) to promote peace, prosperity, security, and the interests of the EU across the globe. It brings together European civil servants, diplomats from EU Member States, national experts and local staff worldwide.

The EEAS supports the High Representative in the exercise of her mandate to steer the Union’s CFSP, including the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP), to represent the EU on issues relating to the CFSP and to chair the Foreign Affairs Council. It also supports her as Vice-President of the Commission with regard to her responsibilities within the Commission, including the coordination of other aspects of the EU’s external action. The EEAS works in close cooperation with the EU Member States, the General Secretariat of the Council, the services of the Commission and the Secretariat General of the European Parliament.

The EEAS Headquarters are in Brussels. It is also responsible for the management of the network of 145 Union Delegations and Offices worldwide. These Diplomatic Representations play a vital role in representing the EU in the country where they are based, in promoting the values and interests of the EU, and in building networks and partnerships. They are responsible for all policy areas of the relationship between the EU and the host country/organisation.

The SG Office supports the Secretary-General in her leadership and overall coordination of the EEAS, ensuring coherence across the Service and alignment with institutional priorities, in close liaison with the Cabinet of the HR/VP. It provides support to the Secretary General including the preparation, coordination, and follow-up of the Secretary-General’s engagements and decision-making. The SG Office manages the Secretary-General’s schedule, coordinates briefings, decisions, and follow-up actions, and ensures the preparation and follow-up of key engagements including inter – institutional meetings, meetings with EU MS as well as internal EEAS matters. It coordinates senior management meetings, facilitates internal and external communication, and maintains day-to-day coordination with other EU institutions, Member States, and relevant external stakeholders.

WE PROPOSE

The EEAS is launching a call for expression of interest for the recruitment of one ASSISTANT (AST2) as Temporary Agent under Article 2(b) of the Conditions of Employment of other servants of the EU1 in accordance with EEAS Decision Admin(2015) 20 on the engagement and use of temporary agents.

Please note that, candidates who have been engaged by the EEAS as non-permanent servants (temporary and contract agents engaged under Article 3b of the CEOS), will be bound by Decision ADMIN(2023) 24 of the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy of 14/07/2023 on the maximum duration of engagement by the European External Action Service of non-permanent staff under successive limited duration contracts of different types, and on the minimum lapse of time between successive contracts under Article 2(e) of the CEOS and repealing the Decision ADMIN(2020) 10 of the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy of 16/07/2020.

- Staff Regulations of Officials (SR) and the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (CEOS). For reference see: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?qid=1570023902133&uri=CELEX:01962R0031-20190101

WE LOOK FOR

A dynamic, proactive and highly motivated colleague with very good communication and organisational skills and with a developed sense of service. He/she will be a critical member of the SG Office, working in an interesting and fast-paced context and will be entrusted with the following administrative tasks, to be carried out in close coordination with another Administrative Assistant:

SG agenda & coordination

- Manage the Secretary-General’s diary, Outlook calendar, forward-planning, and contact lists;
- Screen incoming communication, filter telephone calls, and manage responses to general inquiries for the SG Office;
- Facilitate internal communication and coordination between the SG, EEAS Directorates, EU Institutions, and external interlocutors.

Meetings & visitor management

- Organize internal and external meetings, events, and briefing files for the SG;
- Manage room bookings, submit visitor access requests, and welcome guests and official delegations.

Mission & travel logistics

- Coordinate end-to-end travel logistics for the SG and SG Office, including itineraries, accommodation, visa arrangements, and liaison with Protocol;
- Support annual mission planning, track mission budgets, and process mission orders (MIPS) and reimbursement claims (ARES / representation costs).

Workflow, correspondence & information security

- Contribute to monitoring incoming and outgoing correspondence in ARES, track deadlines, and manage the clearance workflow for briefings (e-brief);
- Maintain internal filing systems and shared drives, securely handling EU Classified Information (EUCI / RUE) according to security regulations.

Office Operations & HR Support

- Liaise with EEAS support services for IT, equipment, furniture, telecom, and office supply procurement;
- Perform additional SG-level administrative tasks as required;
- Support HR administrative duties for the SG, including appraisal, promotion, selection, rotation/mobility, jobs descriptions, training plans and leave and absence management in Sysper2.

LEGAL BASIS

The vacancy is to be filled in accordance with the conditions stipulated under the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (CEOS)1, in accordance with EEAS Decision ADMIN(2015) 20 on the engagement and use of temporary agents

The successful candidate will be offered a contract as Temporary Agent under Article 2(b) of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants (CEOS) at the grade of AST2.

- Staff Regulations of Officials (SR) and the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (CEOS). For reference, see https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?qid=1570023902133&uri=CELEX:01962R0031-20190101

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA

Candidates must meet ALL of the following general and specific conditions on the closing date for online applications:

- Be a national of one of the EU Member States and enjoy full rights as a citizen;
- Meet any obligations imposed on him or her by the laws concerning military service;
- Provide the appropriate character references1 as to their suitability for the performance of their duties;
- Have the capacity to work in languages of the CFSP in writing and orally.
- Post-secondary education attested by a diploma followed by at least 3 years of relevant professional experience directly related to the nature of the duties OR secondary education attested by a diploma giving access to post-secondary education, followed by at least 6 years’ professional experience directly related to the nature of the duties.
- Candidates who, at the time of the application, are EU officials, independently of their administrative status under Article 35 of the SR, cannot request to be recruited as temporary agents. In the case of applications from EU officials on leave for personal grounds, successful candidates will be reinstated into active employment within the meaning of Article 35(a) of the SR.

- criminal records certificate

SELECTION CRITERIA

Candidates should:

- Demonstrate strong capacity for organisation (be able to prioritise, plan, manage time, communicate clearly and concisely);
- Be flexible, cooperative team player and able to multi-task and work autonomously;
- Have the ability to work under time pressure and to deal with urgent issues swiftly and independently;
- Have sound computer skills (MS Office) and good knowledge of standard EU institutions IT workflow applications/ administrative procedures;
- Have very good knowledge of written and verbal English, good knowledge of French (CFSP languages).

Furthermore

- a good knowledge of standard EEAS IT workflow applications/ administrative procedures;
- a good knowledge of Dutch;
- a previous experience in assisting senior management in the EU institutions

would be considered as assets.

EXPRESSION OF INTEREST AND SELECTION PROCEDURE

1. Expression of Interest

Before submitting their application, candidates should carefully check whether they meet all the eligibility criteria in order to avoid exclusion from the selection procedure.

Expressions of interest should be sent by e-mail to the following functional mailbox: AST-STAFFeeas [dot] europa [dot] eu (AST-STAFF[at]eeas[dot]europa[dot]eu)

For the purposes of the e-mail application, the e-mail must have in the subject the following title: "EoI-HQ(AST)-TA2b-AST2-SG Office-job 469618"

Such an expression of interest must be accompanied by:

- an updated Curriculum vitae. Candidates are invited to use the "Europass" CV format (https://europass.cedefop.europa.eu/documents/curriculum-vitae) for their applications.
- a letter of motivation (maximum 2 pages) in either English or in French;
- Declaration of potential conflict of interest form filled in, dated and signed.

The deadline for submission of expressions is 20/10/2026 at 12:00 midday (Brussels time).

For correspondence concerning the selection procedure, please use the following email address (the e-mail must have in the subject the following title: EoI-HQ(AST)-TA2b- AST2-SG Office-job 469618"): AST-STAFFeeas [dot] europa [dot] eu (AST-STAFF[at]eeas[dot]europa[dot]eu)

2. Pre-selection

The selection panel will make a pre-selection on the basis of the qualifications and the professional experience described in the CV and motivation letter.

3. Selection

The candidates who have passed the pre-selection step will be invited for an interview so that the selection panel can evaluate them objectively and impartially based on the selection criteria, as listed in the present call for expression of interest. Additional specific written or oral tests might be organised by the panel. Following a comparative assessment of the merits of the preselected candidates, the selection panel will recommend the name of a candidate to the Authority Authorised to Conclude Contracts of Employment, and possibly, name(s) of other candidate(s) that should be placed on a reserve list valid for maximum 12 months. That list would be used, on the one hand, in case of refusal of the offer or unavailability of the recommended candidate in the present procedure and/or, on the other hand, for other future similar recruitment needs.

Depending on the outcome of future appointment procedure(s) under Article 29 of the SR for a similar profile, EEAS services may, in case no suitable candidates are found among EU officials, have other job opportunities that would involve the recruitment of the Temporary Agents under Article 2(b) of the CEOS. If any, candidates in the above-mentioned reserve list may be contacted by other EEAS services for potential recruitment.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES

The EEAS strives to be a dynamic, respectful and inclusive Service. We value the talent and professional excellence of our staff, and are committed to building an organisation where gender equality and the respect of diversity are core values, as set out in the EEAS Mission Statement and the EEAS Agenda for Diversity and Inclusion. The EEAS is committed to achieving gender balance within its workforce and strives to avoid any form of discrimination during this selection procedure, as per Article 1(d) of the SR. We actively welcome applications from all qualified candidates without any discrimination based on any ground. We commit to recruit candidates with the highest standard of ability, efficiency and integrity, carrying out a selection based on merits required for the post and from the broadest possible geographical basis among the EU Member States.

The EEAS is committed to working with people with disabilities in the terms of the SR. If, by virtue of your medical condition or special needs, you require reasonable accommodation for a part or the entirety of this selection process, please send us an email to EEAS-HQ-APPLICATIONS-ASTeeas [dot] europa [dot] eu (EEAS-HQ-APPLICATIONS-AST[at]eeas[dot]europa[dot]eu). Your request will be treated in strict confidence and no record will be kept. If a candidate with a disability is selected for a vacant post, the EEAS is committed to providing reasonable accommodation in accordance with Article 1(d)(4) of the SR.

All selected candidates are expected to adhere to the Principles of Professional Behaviour of the EEAS, which outline the need for integrity, transparency, respect, professionalism and accountability, and a zero tolerance approach to any form of harassment.

RECRUITMENT

The selected candidate will be recruited as temporary agents under Article 2(b) of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants (CEOS), in accordance with EEAS Decision ADMIN(2015) 20 on the engagement and use of temporary agents.

It is recalled, that if the interest of the service so requires, the selection procedures can be terminated at any stage and the post be filled by a reassignment in accordance with Article 7 of the SR and Article 10 of the CEOS.

Conflict of Interest and security risks

As a matter of policy, applications by individuals who have dual nationality of which one of a non-EU country, will be considered on a case-by-case basis taking account in particular of the functions attributed to the vacant post. The EEAS also examines if there could be a conflict of interest or security risks.

In this context, candidates shall fill with their application a declaration of potential conflict of interest (Annex attached)

Personal Security Clearance

The requested level of security clearance for this post is: SECRET UE/EU SECRET. A description of the EU classified information levels is available under Article 2 of Annex A of the Decision ADMIN(2023) 18 on the security rules of the EEAS1.

The selected candidate should hold, or be in the position to obtain, a valid Personnel Security Clearance (hereafter, the “PSC”)2 issued by the competent authority of the Member State concerned.

Candidates who do not already have a valid PSC will be required to go through the security clearance vetting procedure of their Member State to obtain this clearance in accordance with national laws and regulations and with the procedure laid down in the Decision ADMIN(2025) 42 on Implementing Rules and Procedures for Personnel Security measures for protection of EU Classified Information of 20 November 2025 and in Annex A I of the Decision ADMIN(2023) 18 on the security rules of the EEAS. Until the PSC is issued by the competent authority of the Member State concerned, the selected candidate will not be authorised to access EUCI at the level of CONFIDENTIAL UE/EU CONFIDENTIAL or above, or to participate in any meetings or workflow where EUCI is processed.

Please note that the necessary procedure for obtaining a PSC can be initiated on request of the employer only, and not by the individual candidate.

In case of failure to obtain or renew the required PSC, the AACC may take the appropriate measures in accordance with Article 7 of the Decision ADMIN(2025) 42 on Implementing Rules and Procedures for Personnel Security measures for protection of EU Classified Information of 20 November 2025.

Medical fitness

The selected candidate will be required to undergo a medical fitness examination in accordance with Article 13 of the CEOS.

In case of positive results on the medical fitness examination and after assessment of the PSC conditions, the candidate will be offered a contract as Temporary Agent, Grade AST23 for a duration of 2 years renewable subject to the possibility of extension offered by the EEAS Decision ADMIN(2023) 24 on the maximum duration of engagement.

All member of the temporary staff shall serve initially a nine-month probationary period in accordance with Article 14 CEOS.

- OJ C 263, 26 July 2023, p.16.
- The ‘Personnel Security Clearance’ is defined under point 2 of Annex A I of the Decision ADMIN(2023) 18 on the security rules of the EEAS as “a statement by a competent authority of a Member State which is made following completion of a security investigation conducted by the competent authorities of a Member State and which certifies that an individual may, provided his ‘need-to-know’ has been determined, be granted access to EUCI up to a specified level (CONFIDENTIAL UE/EU CONFIDENTIAL or above) until a specified date; the individual thus described is said to be ‘security cleared’.”
- The basic salaries offered by the EU institutions are set out in Article 66 of the Staff Regulations. The current level, can be accessed via the link: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=OJ:C_202506564. A number of factors are taken into account in calculating your pay

postings.title: Administrative Assistant - with the Clean Hydrogen Joint Under (Grade AST3)
postings.description:
- JOB PROFILE AND DUTIES

2.1 JOB PROFILE

The jobholder will report to the Head of Unit for Finance and Administration. The successful applicant will be responsible for providing overall administrative and logistical support to the Programme Office team.

2.2 DUTIES

The jobholder will be part of a team responsible for the administrative and financial support to the Clean Hydrogen JU Programme Office. He/she will perform the following tasks:

- Financial initiation of transactions for the JU’s administrative expenditure and revenue (roles of data entry agent and financial initiating agent),
- Supporting the Programme Office teams in calls for proposals and evaluations and in project reviews: management of the expert contracts and payments, organisation of the expert panel meetings;
- Standard secretariat tasks:
- Administration of internal and external physical and electronic mail, including in a set of functional mailboxes;
- Taking notes and minutes of relevant meetings, including Governance meetings;
- Coordination common calendars;
- Reception of visitors;
- Electronic registration and archiving of documents,
- Supporting travel administration;
- Drafting of routine correspondence.

- Organisation of meetings, seminars and conferences, in support to Governance and Advisory Bodies, or to meetings in the JU’s premises involving external participants: including invitations to participants, room reservations, logistics, catering and reimbursement of expenses;
- General administrative and logistics support to the office;
- Deputising for other secretary during his/her absences;

To perform his/her duties, the jobholder shall establish good working relationships with colleagues and positively contribute to effective teamwork.

The jobholder may undertake additional tasks e.g. related to financial management, as required in the interest of the service and appropriate to his/her expertise.

- QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE REQUIRED

Candidates will be considered for the selection phase based on the following formal criteria, which must be fulfilled by the deadline for applications:

3.1 ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA

The Administrative Assistant will be selected based on the following criteria:

- A level of education of at least;
- a level of post-secondary education attested by a diploma, or
- a level of secondary education attested by a diploma giving access to post-secondary education, and appropriate professional experience of at least three years
- where justified in the interests of the service, professional training or professional experience of an equivalent level.

- At least 6 (six) years of professional experience relevant to the activities;
- Thorough knowledge of one of the languages of the European Union and a satisfactory knowledge of another language of the European Union to the extent necessary for the performance of his/her duties; the working language in the Clean Hydrogen JU is English;
- Be a national of one of the Member States of the European Union;
- Enjoy full rights as a citizen;
- Have fulfilled any obligations imposed on him/her by the laws of their home country concerning military service;
- Meet the character requirements for the duties involved;
- Be physically fit to perform his/her duties.

3.2 SELECTION CRITERIA

Candidates selected on the basis of the above eligibility criteria will then be evaluated according to the following selection criteria. Failure to comply with the eligibility and essential selection criteria will result in a disqualification of the applicant concerned.

Essential

- Relevance of the academic background and/or of the professional experience to the duties and responsibilities described under key accountabilities; preference will be given to qualifications acquired in the fields of finance and business administration;
- By the closing date for applications candidates must have acquired at least 6 (six) years of professional experience (following award of the diploma) relevant to the position (traineeships and internships are not counted in the relevant professional experience);
- Very good analytical, communication and problem-solving skills; ability to track and follow up a variety of tasks in parallel;
- Good knowledge of the European Union institutions, funds source structure of the EU budget and the EU’s framework programmes;
- Excellent organisational skills;
- Good practical knowledge of the administrative and financial rules of the EU and their legal basis, and of their application in financial, accounting and audit processes;
- Practical experience of ICT administrative and financial management tools as used in the EU institutions;
- Proven ability to work in a team and in a multicultural environment, and ability to motivate others;
- Very good command of both oral and written English;
- Proficiency in the use of standard MS Office applications, email, internet and strong aptitude for working with IT tools;
- A strong sense of ownership, accountability, responsibility, initiative and self-motivation;
- Experience working in a multicultural, international environment.

Advantageous:

It is desirable for the selected candidate to have the following:

- Understanding of the Joint Undertakings environment.

- SELECTION PROCEDURE

A Selection Committee, appointed by the Appointing Authority of the Clean Hydrogen JU assesses / evaluates the applications in accordance with the eligibility and selection criteria outlined in the vacancy notice and establishes a short list of applicants invited for an interview and a written test.

The Selection Committee will interview the shortlisted applicants. These applicants will also sit a written test related to the field of duties. Following this, the Selection Committee will establish a reserve list of suitable candidates to be approved by the Executive Director.

Candidates are reminded that the Selection Committee’s work is confidential. It is strictly forbidden for candidates to make direct or indirect contact with its members or to ask anybody to do so on their behalf.

The number of candidates invited for an interview will be limited to a maximum of 15.

- RESERVE LIST AND APPOINTMENT

The Executive Director may decide to interview the candidates before establishment of the reserve list and/or appointment.

The reserve list may be used in order to fulfil positions within the Clean Hydrogen JU.

Candidates should note that inclusion on the reserve list does not guarantee recruitment. Recruitment will be based on availability of posts and budget.

The reserve list for this post will be valid for a period of two years from the date of its establishment and may be extended at the discretion of the Appointing Authority of the Clean Hydrogen JU.

- CONTRACTUAL CONDITIONS

A contract offer will be made as a temporary agent, pursuant to Article 2(f) of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Communities, to which he/she will be subject, for a period of three years. The contract may be renewed in accordance with the legal basis applicable to the joint undertaking.

The successful candidate will undergo an initial probationary period of 9 months.

Remuneration will be based on the Union scale of salaries. Pay is subject to Union tax and other deductions laid down in the Staff Regulations. Remuneration is, however, exempt from any national taxation.

For the position of Administrative Assistant, the grade is AST 3. The basic monthly salary of a temporary agent in the first step at AST 3 level, before any deductions or allowances, is EUR 4 806,17.

The place of employment is Brussels, Belgium, where the Clean Hydrogen JU has its official seat.

For any further information on contractual and working conditions, please refer to the Staff Regulations of Officials of the European Communities and its Conditions of Employment of Other Servants (CEOS) of the European Communities, which is available on the following web page: Staff regulations CEOS

For reasons related to the Clean Hydrogen JU’s operational requirements, the candidate will be required to be available at short notice (maximum 3 months).

- DECLARATION OF COMMITMENT TO SERVE PUBLIC INTEREST INDEPENDENTLY

The successful candidate will be required to make a declaration of commitment to act independently in the public interest and to make a declaration in relation to interests which might be considered prejudicial to his/her independence. Candidates must confirm their willingness to do so in their application.

- EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

The Clean Hydrogen JU applies a policy of equal opportunity for men and women and accepts applications without distinction on grounds of sex, race, colour, ethnic or social origin, genetic characteristics, and language, religious, political or other convictions or opinions, financial situation, disability, age, sexual orientation, marital status or family situation.

- SUBMISSION OF APPLICATIONS

For applications to be valid, candidates must submit an online application via the vacancies portal: vacancy portal.

Candidates are requested to:

1. complete the online application form - to access the right form, candidates should select the vacancy for which they wish to apply;

2. upload a letter of motivation;

3. upload a Curriculum Vitae (CV), preferably in the European CV format http://europass.cedefop.europa.eu).

For the letter of motivation and the CV, only Word documents (.doc or .docx) or PDF documents (.pdf) will be accepted. The maximum file size is 2 MB.

IMPORTANT: for each position, any new application made by a candidate with the same e-mail address will automatically erase and replace the previous application for that position.

The application will be rejected if the dossier is incomplete.

Candidates are advised to apply using e-mail address that will remain valid for several months: candidates that will leave their job in the coming months are advised not to use their professional e-mail address.

Supporting documents (e.g. certified copies of degrees/diplomas, references, proof of experience, etc.) should not be sent at this point but must be submitted at a later stage as indicated below.

In order to facilitate the selection process, application documents as well as all communications to candidates concerning this vacancy will be in English.

Application forms sent by e-mail, fax or post will not be accepted.

Candidates are asked to report any potential change of contact details without delay, to the following e-mail address: recruitmentclean-hydrogen [dot] europa [dot] eu (recruitment[at]clean-hydrogen[dot]europa[dot]eu).

Please remember to quote the reference of the vacancy for which you have applied in all correspondence: CleanH2JU/Administrative Assistant/2026.

Candidates should assess and check before submitting their application whether they fulfil all the requirements as specified in the vacancy notice, particularly in terms of qualifications and relevant professional experience.

Should candidates be invited for an interview, in order for the application to be considered complete, they must bring with them on the day of interview originals or certified photocopies of the supporting documents for their education qualifications and employment (diplomas, working certificates, etc.). All documentary evidence of professional experience must indicate both start and end dated of previous positions and the start date of the position held currently, full time or part time work has to be indicated as well. Freelance or self-employed candidates must provide either a copy of the entry in the relevant trade register, or any official document (for example a tax revenue) showing clearly the length of the relevant professional experience.

The Clean Hydrogen JU has the right to disqualify candidates who fail to submit all the required documents on the date of interview.

As a candidate you are to be informed that in a later stage of the recruitment process a mandatory medical analysis and physical check-up is done with a selected medical service.

Closing date for the submission is 15 November 2026, at 23:59 CET.

- APPEAL PROCEDURE

A candidate who feels that he/she has been treated incorrectly may ask to have his/her application reconsidered by sending, within 20 calendar days of the date of notification, a request for review via e-mail to: recruitmentclean-hydrogen [dot] europa [dot] eu (recruitment[at]clean-hydrogen[dot]europa[dot]eu). The candidate should quote the number of the selection procedure concerned and address the request to the Chairman of the Selection Committee.

The Selection Committee will reconsider the application and notify the candidate of its decision within 45 calendar days of receipt of the request.

If the candidate considers that he/she has been adversely affected by a particular decision, he/she can lodge a complaint under Article 90(2) of the Staff Regulations of Officials of the European Communities and the Conditions of employment of other servants of the European Communities (CEOS), at the following address:

Executive Director

Clean Hydrogen JU

WA, TO 56-60

B-1049 Brussels

Belgium

The complaint must be lodged within 3 months. The time limit for initiating this type of procedure (see the Staff Regulations as modified by Council Regulation No 723/2004 of 22 March 2004 published in the Official Journal of the European Union L 124 of 27 April 2004 – http://europa.eu/eur-lex) starts to run from the time the candidate is first informed of the outcome of the recruitment procedure).

If the complaint is rejected the candidate may bring a case under Article 236 of the EC treaty and Article 91 of the Staff Regulations and the CEOS before:

The European Union Civil Service Tribunal

Postal Address:

L-2925 Luxembourg

The Appointing Authority does not have the power to amend the assessment decisions of the Selection Committee. The Court has consistently held that the wide discretion enjoyed by Selection Committee is not subject to review by the Court unless rules which govern the proceedings of the Selection Committee have been infringed.

It is also possible to complain to the European Ombudsman pursuant to Article 195(1) of the Treaty establishing the European Community and in accordance with the conditions laid down in the Decision of the European Parliament of 9 March 1994 on the Staff Regulations and the general conditions governing the performance of the Ombudsman’s duties, published in the Official Journal of the European Union L 113 of 4 May 1994:

European Ombudsman

1 Avenue du Président Robert Schuman – BP 403

F-67001 Strasbourg Cedex

Complaints made to the Ombudsman have no suspense effect on the period laid down in the Articles 90(2) and 91 of the Staff Regulations for lodging, respectively, a complaint or an appeal with the European Union Civil Service Tribunal under Article 236 of the EC Treaty.

- DATA PROTECTION

The purpose of processing of the data you submit is to manage your application in view of a possible secondment to the Clean Hydrogen JU. The personal information we request from you will be processed in line with Regulation (EU) 2018/1725 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2018 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data by the Union Institutions, Bodies, Offices and Agencies and on the free movement of such data, and repealing Regulation (EC) No 45/2001 and Decision No 1247/2002/EC Text with EEA reference.

For more explanations on data protection please see the privacy statement here.

- ^

Only diplomas and certificates that have been awarded in EU member states or that are the subject of equivalence certificates issued by authorities in the said Member States shall be taken into consideration

- ^

Prior to the appointment, the successful candidate will be asked to provide a certificate issued by the competent authority attesting the absence of any criminal record.

postings.title: Administrative Coordinator
Agent logistique
postings.description:
About us

L'Office pour les Infrastructures et la Logistique de Bruxelles (OIB) a pour mission l'exécution de toutes les activités liées à l'hébergement du personnel, à la gestion des infrastructures sociales et à la logistique de la Commission à Bruxelles ainsi que des infrastructures sociales sur le site d'Ispra

Le secteur OIB.RE.3.001 « Équipes de proximité » appartient à l’unité OIB.RE.3 « Énergie, EMAS, et support logistique » au sein du Département OIB.RE « Gestion des biens immobiliers ».

Le secteur OIB. RE.3.001 comprend environ 140 agents logistiques répartis sur 12 équipes « LPT » (Logistics Proximity Teams), une équipe de coordination centrale et une équipe d’agents de support logistique en poste au Berlaymont, chargée de l’assistance aux réunions, salle de conférence (pour la Présidente, le Collège des commissaires et le Secrétaire Général.

La mission de ce secteur est d’offrir un service opérationnel en contact direct avec les clients.

About the role

Le secteur OIB.RE.3.001 recherches 5 agents de support logistique GFI (AC3a) pour constituer une liste de réserve afin de renforcer ses équipes. Ces agents seront notamment chargés d'assurer un service VIP au sein de l'équipe responsable de l'assistance aux Cabinets, aux organisateurs et aux participants de réunions.

Vos tâches principales seront :

- Préparer, organiser et maintenir l’ordre des salles de conférence du Berlaymont, en assurant un service prioritaire pour les réunions du Collège ainsi que celles impliquant la Présidente, les Chefs de Cabinet et le Secrétaire générale.
- Assurer la mise en place logistique et le bon déroulement des réunions avant, pendant et après leur tenue, en veillant à la disponibilité des fournitures et au respect des besoins opérationnels.
- Gérer l’approvisionnement et la distribution du matériel nécessaire en salle, notamment l’eau, le papier, les gobelets et autres consommables.
- Réceptionner, trier et distribuer les documents et le courrier, y compris la gestion ducourrier DHL, tout en utilisant efficacement les outils informatiques liés à la fonction.
- Accueillir, informer et orienter les participants aux conférences et prendre en charge les visiteurs VIP dans le cadre des visites officielles au sein de la Commission européenne.
- Assurer le suivi opérationnel des réunions et de la communication interne, notamment via la boîte fonctionnelle (FMB), l’application de gestion des salles, l’élaboration du planning.
- Contribuer au bon fonctionnement général du service, en assurant ponctuellement le « backup » des équipes logistiques, en mettant à jour les porte-noms et informations d’affichage, et ensignalant toute anomalie de sécurité, d’hygiène ou d’ordre technique aux services compétents.

Qualifications, experience and skills

Obligatoire: Une expérience professionnelle d’au moins 2 ans dans le domaine du support logistique (huissiers ou équivalent)

Souhaité: La maîtrise des outils informatiques utilisés par les agents de support logistique (MS Office) : Excel, Outlook, Word. Une expérience auprès de clients VIP.

Qualités personnelles requises et évaluées au cours de l’entretien:

Excellente communication, orientation services et clients.

Conscience professionnelle, souci du détail et de la précision.

Flexibilité (ouverture à l'égard de nouvelles exigences, de nouvelles technologies, de nouvelles cultures, de nouvel environnement, etc…).

Capacité de la planification.

Persévérance et résistance au stress, flexibilité (heures de travail atypiques) et attention aux détails.

Capacité de travailler dans une équipe de manière proactive.

Compétences diplomatiques, sensibilité et attention aux différences personnelles.Confidentialité.

Langues: La connaissance du français et/ou de l’anglais constitue un avantage.

How to express your interest?

Afin de garantir l'égalité d'accès à tous, la Commission recrute à partir d'une base de données permanente de candidatures spontanées. Le présent appel à manifestation d'intérêt vise à aider les recruteurs à identifier les candidats potentiellement intéressés dans cette base de données.

En pratique, pour manifester votre intérêt, veuillez suivre les deux étapes suivantes :

Si vous n'êtes pas encore inscrit dans la base de données ouverte en permanence d'EPSO, veuillez le faire à l'adresse suivante : CAST Permanent. Veuillez sélectionner parmi les procédures de sélection de l'agent contractuel le profil permanent CAST qui correspond le mieux à votre formation et à votre expérience.

postings.title: Case Handler Officer - Communication
postings.description:
About us (“We are”)

IDOC (the Investigation and Disciplinary Office of the Commission) is a Directorate within DG HR that mainly deals with administrative inquiries and disciplinary proceedings. IDOC reports directly to the Director General of DG HR and it is composed of a team of motivated, friendly and hard-working legal officers and assistants. Our mission is to ensure that staff members comply with their statutory obligations. This is achieved through the conduct of formal procedures, in a fair, transparent and timely manner and in accordance with the rules on data protection as well as through outreach programs, aiming at increasing awareness among the staff about the binding obligations enshrined in the Staff Regulations and related legislation]

About the role (“We propose”)

If several positions are advertised for similar job profiles, please add the number of vacant jobs. A highly engaging role. As Case Handle Officer you will be responsible for conducting internal administrative inquiries, pre disciplinary and disciplinary proceedings concerning the obligations applicable to Commission staff members. Administrative inquiries aim to establish the facts and determine whether obligations laid down in the Staff Regulations have been breached. Disciplinary proceedings are initiated where there is evidence that such obligations have been breached, whether intentionally or through negligence. The cases handled cover a broad range of matters, including harassment, unauthorised outside activities, non-respect of the rules on time-management, offences under national criminal law established by the national Courts and serious misconduct in private life. You will contribute to the strengthening of the ethical culture in the Commission through presentations, awareness-raising activities and outreach programs.

Qualifications, experience and skills (“We look for”)
We are looking for a an experienced, well organized and motivated staff member, with a strong legal background and previous experience in investigations and disciplinary proceedings, to join our existing multi-disciplinary team of case handlers.

Our future colleague should have good people skills and the ability to:

- conduct inquiries proactively;
- propose solutions to upcoming questions;
- ssist the Appointing Authority in disciplinary proceedings;
- liaise with other services including OLAF, EPPO, the Secretariat-General, the Legal Service and the Data Protection Officer; - work autonomously as well as in a team;
- analyse complex situations;
- carry out horizontal tasks pertaining to the work of IDOC, such as outreach program activities, whistleblowing policy, etc.

A high level of legal expertise, a good knowledge of legal proceedings and practical aspects of investigations, as well as of the relevant rules on data protection, is essential. S/he should have excellent communication and drafting skills in both English and French. Knowledge of other languages would be an advantage.

The nature of the post requires a very strict attitude in relation to the protection of personal data and the constraints that this imposes on daily working life. A good capacity for teamwork, a well-developed sense of discretion, service-mindedness and a high level of integrity and ethical awareness are essential.

How to express your interest?

You should send your documents in a single pdf in the following order:
1. your CV

2. completed application form.

Please send these documents by the publication deadline to HR-MAIL-IDOCec [dot] europa [dot] eu (HR-MAIL-IDOC[at]ec[dot]europa[dot]eu) indicating the selection reference HR/COM/2026/1799 in the subject.

No applications will be accepted after the publication deadline.

postings.description:
Job Summary

Under the supervision of the Head of Unit, the Communications and External Relations officer acts as a team leader for COMMs and RELEX teams. He/she is responsible for the development and implementation of CEPOL's communications sub-strategy as well as CEPOL's external relations strategy.

He/she is responsible for the planning, implementation, monitoring and reporting of communication activities internally and externally, in line with the Agency's communications sub-strategy, and for CEPOL's external action, including Working Arrangements, cooperation with JHA Agencies and international organisations, relations with EU Member States and third countries, and support to CEPOL management for high-level meetings and institutional engagements. The post also includes steering, the activities of the Brussels Liaison Office. Frequent short-term missions within and outside the EU are required.

Key accountabilities

- Develop and implement CEPOL's communications sub-strategy and external relations strategy in an integrated manner, ensuring consistency between the Agency's public messaging and its institutional/diplomatic engagement; contribute to the implementation of the CEPOL Strategy overall, including through joint stakeholder mapping.
- Maintain relations with press, media, and other key external partners; draft and update Working Arrangements.
- Act as single point of contact (SPOC) for EU Member States, EU institutions, and relevant authorities in non-EU countries; support CEPOL in strengthening ties with other EU Agencies, particularly within the JHA field (including representing CEPOL in the JHA Agencies' Network).
- Oversee website and social media management and the development/production of CEPOL communications materials, ensuring alignment with the Agency's brand identity and coordination with external relations messaging and institutional engagements.
- Oversee the intranet landing page and maintain the electronic archive of dossiers.
- Draft analytical and periodical reports, correspondence, briefing notes, and communications materials, in support of both public communication and institutional/diplomatic engagement.
- Contribute to planning, coordination, and execution of CEPOL events and high-level engagements, integrating both communications (visibility, media) and external-relations (institutional, protocol) dimensions.
- Monitor the activities of the Brussels Liaison Office and provide back-up when needed to ensure business continuity.
- Manage the teams budget allocation and expenditure; oversee contracts and service providers.
- Manage specific projects and tools related to CEPOL's external action and communications.
- Coordinate the staff assigned to Communications and External Relations activities.
- Other tasks as requested by the Line Manager.

Eligibility criteria

In addition, in order to be eligible the candidate must:

- Be a national of a Member State of the Union;
- Be entitled to his or her full rights as a citizen;
- Have fulfilled any obligations imposed by the applicable laws on military service;
- Meet the character requirements for the duties involved;
- Be physically fit to perform the duties linked to the post; and
- Have a thorough knowledge (min. level C1) of one of the languages of the Union and a satisfactory knowledge (min. level B2) of another language of the Union. As the official language of the Agency is English one of the before mentioned languages has to be English.

Education

Level of education which corresponds to completed university studies of at least three years attested by a diploma in the field of Communications, Public Relations, International Relations, Diplomacy, Political studies, Internal Security or a related field;

In the interest of the service, professional training or equivalent (such as CIPR - Chartered Institute of Public Relations or similar, or graduating from a police or law enforcement education institution) and after having completed the training, at least the number of years of relevant professional experience indicated below:

Duration of professional trainingProfessional experienceMore than 6 months and up to 1 year4 yearsMore than 1 year and up to 2 years3 yearsMore than 2 years and up to 3 years2 yearsMore than 3 years1 year

Professional Experience

In addition to the above, at least 3 years of relevant professional experience gained after obtaining the diploma or after completed the professional training with the experience linked to the training.

Working conditions

A contract offer will be made as a member of the Temporary Agent staff of the agency in accordance with the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Communities for a five years period, which may be renewed for additional 5 years. The third contract will be for an indefinite period. The successful candidate will be recruited as Communications and External Relations Officer - AD6.

The basic monthly net pay for this post is EUR 4,046.37 (Step 1) or EUR 4,197.05 (Step 2). The correction coefficient (on the date of publication of this vacancy notice) is 76,6% for Hungary and is already taken in consideration for these amounts.

The step is determined on the basis of professional experience gained after obtaining the diploma of an education required for the position and in line with applicable implementing rules.

In addition, based on personal situation, the following allowances might be granted:

- Expatriation or foreign residence allowance: 16% or 4% of the basic pay.
- Annual travel allowance: staff who are entitled to the expatriation (16%) or foreign residence (4%) allowance are entitled to be paid each calendar year a sum representing the cost of travel from the place of employment to the place of origin for themselves and, if they are entitled to the household allowance, for their spouse and dependents (over the age of 2)
- Household allowance
- Allowance for a dependent child or person treated as such:
- Pre-school allowance:
- Education allowance:
- School fees: paid by CEPOL for dependent children who joined the staff member in changing the residence to fully respect the article 20 of the Staff Regulations. The school shall be considered as non-fee paying and the staff member concerned shall not receive the education allowance mentioned in the bullet point(s) above.

The costs covered by CEPOL shall be:

- The registration and attendance fees at international schools
- The transportation costs
- Excluding all other costs as described on the Commission decision C(2004)131-53-2004 on general implementing provisions for the grant of the education allowance.

In addition, CEPOL will provide benefits and entitlements in line with those of European Union Civil Servants. Such entitlements will be established based on the necessary documents provided by the newly recruited staff member upon taking up duty with CEPOL.

The successful candidate shall undergo a probation period of 9 months.

For reasons related to CEPOL’s operational requirements, the candidate may be required to be available at short notice.

Additional information

The highest scoring candidates exceeding the threshold defined in advance by the Selection Committee shall be invited for online interview and remote written test. Maximum number of candidates to be invited for interview shall not exceed 12. The interview/written test are planned to take place in the first week of December 2026.

The information provided in applications is subject to EU legislation on protection of personal data and confidentiality of information.

Privacy statements: Privacy statement for processing of personal data related to recruitment

Only candidates who achieve 65% of the total scores available for the interview and written test might be included in a Reserve List. The reserve list will be valid until 31 December 2028 and may be extended by the decision of the Appointing Authority of CEPOL. (Please be aware that placement on a reserve list in no way guarantees future employment at CEPOL.) Prior to being offered a post, candidates may be required to undergo further evaluation by CEPOL.

Essential Criteria

- Minimum 3 years’ experience in developing and implementing integrated communications and external-relations strategies.
- Minimum 3 years’ professional experience in communications, in the public sector, including developing and managing digital and print communications, website content, social media/press and publication.
- Minimum 3 years’ experience in managing high-level institutional and international stakeholder relations and delivering high-level events and engagements (please describe the duration, your role, which aspects/parts you covered, etc.).
- Minimum 3 years’ experience in managing teams, budgets, contracts, projects and operational activities. (Please describe your exact role, budget managed, size of the team coordinated, volume of the projects, etc.)

Advantageous Criteria

- Experience in the field of EU internal security and with cooperating with Justice and Home Affaires Agencies.
- Previous professional experience in protocol, including the organization and coordination of official events, high-level meetings, visits, ceremonies, and the application of institutional or diplomatic protocol procedures.
- Experience in drafting formal administrative reports, statements and speeches, statements, briefing notes, etc. (Please provide examples, list types).
- Experience in analyzing complex political content, policies at EU level. (please provide examples).

Link to vacancy

The Court’s mission
The Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) lies at the heart of European justice. As the judicial authority of the Union, it works in close collaboration with national jurisdictions of the Member States to ensure the consistent interpretation and application of the EU Treaties and law. As an employer, the CJEU strives for excellence and values multilingualism, inclusiveness, diversity, and collaboration.
Who will be your team?
The Cybersecurity team of the Court of Justice (CJEU) is reporting to the Director of IT. The mission of the team is to protect the Court's assets against cybersecurity threats and to ensure end-to-end data security and protection. The team is responsible for the holistic cybersecurity program covering govern, identify, protect, detect, respond and recover functions. The team is divided into the sections Operations, Risk-Compliance and Solutions.
What will your contribution be?
We are looking for cybersecurity experts in all three sections to strengthen our Cybersecurity team. You will drive secure architecture implementation, ensure risk and compliance management, and/or contribute to operational cyber‑defence:
Implement, configure and operate technical cybersecurity controls (access management, logging, monitoring, vulnerability scanning, etc.) in line with the Cybersecurity Regulation.
Monitor systems and networks, detect anomalies and respond to incidents, supporting containment, eradication and recovery of services.
Identify, assess and remediate vulnerabilities, develop secure configuration baselines and monitor patch‑management activities.
Support internal risk‑management, governance and compliance, ensuring alignment with the Court’s Cybersecurity policies and the Cybersecurity regulation.
Collaborate with the IT teams to align security measures with the overall security architecture, integrate requirements into projects and continuously improve controls.
Are you who we are looking for?
Basic qualifications:
Be a national of one of the Member States of the European Union (EU).
AD: University studies of at least 3 years attested by a diploma.
AST: Post-secondary studies attested by a diploma, or secondary education giving access to post-secondary studies with at least 3 years of appropriate professional experience.
A thorough knowledge of one of the EU’s official languages and a satisfactory knowledge of another. For working reasons, good knowledge of English is Knowledge of French is considered as an advantage. English is mainly essential for collaborating on interinstitutional level, drafting and processing technical documents and French would help coordinating between services.
Desirable qualifications:
Certifications in cybersecurity or information security (CISSP, CISM, GIAC, ISO27000, SANS, etc.).
At least 3 years of professional experience in cybersecurity/information security or in information technology with a focus on security technologies.
Excellent analysis and problem solving skills.
Very good prioritisation and organisational skills.

Work from home possibilities
Multicultural environment
Attractive remuneration and allowances
Life-long learning
Flexible working hours
Sports centre

postings.description:
VACANCY NOTICE - CONTRACT AGENT
Job title  Data and Business Process Analyst
Reference  EC-2026-BUDG-523121
Application deadline  26.10.2026 - 12.00 (noon, Brussels time)
Directorate-General (full name)  DG BUDGET
Unit  Chief Risk Officer Unit
Place of assignment  Brussels
Domain  Economics, Finance and Statistics
Contract type and  Contract Agent 3b
Function Group  FG IV

About us

The Chief Risk Officer (CRO) is an independent function, overseeing the financial
risks from the Union’s financial operations, such as the borrowing and debt
management operations, assets under management operations, lending operations
and budgetary guarantees.

The Union’s financial operations have expanded significantly – in volume and scope
– over the course of the present Multiannual Financial Framework. Loans, budgetary
guarantees, and financing of EU policies through issuance of debt securities have
been used on large scale to fund responses to emerging challenges and successive
crises. The implementation of these financial operations expose the Union to a
variety of financial risks, including credit, market, liquidity, operational, reputational,
compliance. The financial risks arising from the implementation of the Union’s
financial operations should be properly identified, mitigated, managed, and reported.
The risk management framework should be robust and provide a comprehensive,
rigorous, and independent capacity for supervising the financial risks arising across
all Union’s financial operations undertaken. The framework should ensure that
Union’s financial operations should be conducted in a manner consistent with the
highest standards of integrity and sound financial and risk management.

The Commission tasked the CRO as the second line of defence, with the
development and implementation of the Commission’s risk management framework.
Supported by a risk management unit, the CRO is responsible for ensuring robust
governance, effective risk management and oversight of the financial risks
associated with the Union’s financial operations. The CRO works in close
cooperation with the Directorates-General responsible for the Union’s financial
operations, acting in their capacity as first line of defence. The CRO chairs the Risk
and Compliance Committee, which supports the CRO developing the risk framework

and the management of the financial risks arising from the Union’s financial
operations.

The CRO function is hosted by Directorate-General for Budget (DG BUDG), which
is the central service of the European Commission responsible for the preparation
and implementation of the annual and multiannual budget of the European Union. It
consists of about 600 staff and is made up of seven directorates based in Brussels
and in Luxembourg. The staff members come from all EU countries with various
professional expertise: accounting, economics, finance, business, programming,
audit, law, communications, human resources, European administration, and other
fields.

CRO unit is structured into two sectors – Sector one focused on risk oversight of
budgetary guarantees and financial assistance and Sector two responsible for risk
oversight of borrowing operations and asset under management. A dedicated
compliance function provides compliance and operational risk oversight.

The CRO has developed an in-house risk management IT tool to support the
assessment, monitoring and reporting of risks arising from EU financial operations.
The tool incorporates several quantitative models covering credit, market and
funding risks, which constitute a key pillar of the Commission’s risk management
framework.

About the role

We offer an exciting and challenging opportunity within the Chief Risk Officer Unit,
as a Data and Business Process Management Expert who will be assigned to the
sector responsible for borrowing operations and asset under management.
The risk management IT tool is developed, maintained and continually enhanced
by the CRO Unit. It is used by several Commission services and developments and
updates are performed in close collaboration with the first line of defence. Looking
ahead, key challenges include the integration of artificial intelligence (AI)
capabilities, the harmonisation of currently fragmented databases, and the
development of new risk management functionalities to ensure that the
Commission’s risk management capabilities continue to evolve in response to a
changing financial and risk environment.
In this role, you will play a central part in ensuring that the data used by risk
management and by other stakeholders, relying on risk management outputs, meet
best-in-class standards in terms of quality, consistency and harmonisation. You will
ensure that data is reliable, readily available and suitable for consolidated risk
reporting and quantitative risk analysis.
The position also serves as the key interface between risk analysts, quantitative risk
officers responsible for developing risk methodologies and models, and the IT teams
responsible for implementing these models within the Commission's information

systems. As such, you will act as the primary point of contact within the CRO Unit
for coordinating business requirements with IT colleagues and managing the
maintenance and further development of risk management IT solutions. More
specifically, your responsibilities will include:
- Design, maintain and further develop the corporate database used to consolidate
all input data related to borrowing operations and asset under management. The
work should be performed in close cooperation with the first line of defence.
- Ensure the quality, accuracy, consistency and completeness of the data stored
across the various systems, and develop the data governance framework required
to support effective data management, monitoring, traceability and auditability.
- Support risk analysts and quantitative risk officers by ensuring that high-quality
data is permanently available and fit for purpose.
- Ensure, in collaboration with IT colleagues, the integration of adequate AI
solutions for risk management purposes, such as in the IT Risk Management tool.
- Support the implementation of new risk methodologies, quantitative models and
reporting solutions by identifying, collecting and preparing any additional data
required for their development and deployment.
- Act as the primary liaison between the Chief Risk Officer Unit and the IT teams
responsible for risk management IT solutions, analysing and validating business
requirements and their impact on data, processes and systems, coordinating their
end-to-end implementation from development and user acceptance testing to
deployment, and ensuring that delivered solutions meet the Unit’s business needs.

Qualifications, experience and skills

Experience & skills:
- Minimum 5 years of relevant professional experience in data management,
business analysis and/or IT project management, preferably gained in the financial
sector or professional services: knowledge of data management, including data
quality, governance, lineage, harmonisation and controls is a requirement.
- Experience with large and complex datasets, data modelling and database
structures, preferably involving financial and risk data.
- Ability to use AI and automation tools for data management and analytics,
including data preparation, quality control, reconciliation, anomaly detection and
workflow automation, with appropriate validation and human oversight.
- Experience in designing, maintaining or improving business processes and data
management frameworks in a complex organisational environment.
- Experience in coordinating IT projects or acting as a liaison between business
users, data specialists and IT development teams. Experience in translating
business requirements into functional specifications for IT developments.

- Excellent Excel skills; experience with Power BI, Python, SQL or equivalent data
and analytics tools would be an advantage.
- Knowledge of financial products such as fixed income and equity instruments in
the context of borrowing and asset management operations is considered as an
advantage. Knowledge of financial risk management would also be an asset.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving and project coordination skills, with the ability
to manage multiple stakeholders and priorities.
- Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and
deliver under tight deadlines.

Education:
- University degree in information systems, data science, statistics, finance and
another relevant discipline
- Professional certifications such as FRM (Financial Risk Manager), CFA
(Chartered Financial Analyst) or PRMIA (Professional Risk Manager) are a plus.

How to express your interest?

You should send your documents in a single pdf in the following order:

  1. Your CV  2. Completed application form

Please send these documents by the publication deadline to BUDG-MAILBOX-
CRO@ec.europa.eu indicating the selection reference EC-2026-BUDG-523121
Eligibility
For eligibility, please consult this page with all the information needed.
