The European Institute for Gender Equality (EIGE)1 invites applications with a view to establish a reserve list for the post of Seconded National Expert – Gender-Based Violence (GBV).
The registration of applications begins on 6 October 2026 and will close on 11 November 2026 at 13:30 Eastern European Time.
The Agency
Based in Vilnius, Lithuania, EIGE is a decentralised agency of the European Union (EU) entrusted with specific objectives envisaged to contribute and strengthen the promotion of gender equality.
To achieve its goals, the Agency collects and analyses comparable and reliable information at EU level and develops appropriate methodological tools for the integration of gender equality into all EU policies. It fosters the exchange of good practices and dialogue between stakeholders and raises EU citizen awareness of this policy area by providing technical assistance to EU institutions, in particular the European Commission, as well as the authorities of the Member States.
In the course of its work to promote and strengthen gender equality, EIGE supports policymakers with high-quality research and comparable data relevant to their work.
Job description
Context
Combating gender-based violence (GBV) is one of the European Commission’s policy priorities, as set out in the Roadmap for Women’s Rights and the Gender Equality Strategy 2026–2030.
In 2023, the European Union ratified the Council of Europe Convention on preventing and combating violence against women and domestic violence (CETS No. 210), known as the Istanbul Convention. In May 2024, Directive (EU) 2024/1385 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 May 2024 on combating violence against women and domestic violence was adopted.
The Directive criminalises at EU level certain forms of violence against women, including specific forms of online violence, and requires Member States to put in place comprehensive measures concerning prevention, protection, access to justice, support, coordination and cooperation between authorities. It also establishes requirements for the collection, development, production and dissemination of statistics on violence against women and domestic violence.
These developments have increased the demand from EU institutions and Member States for evidence, expertise and practical support to strengthen institutional responses to violence against women and domestic violence. They also require robust, comparable and high-quality data to inform effective policies and monitor progress.
EIGE is mandated to support Member States and EU institutions through evidence-based research, data collection and analysis, development of common standards and indicators, and the provision of gender equality expertise.
Against this background, EIGE is establishing a Seconded National Expert (SNE) vacancy with two complementary profiles:
Profile 1 – Statistical/Data
Profile 2 – Legal/Policy
The purpose of the vacancy is to strengthen EIGE’s capacity and expertise in gender-based violence and gender equality, both in relation to ongoing work and to emerging and future needs arising from EU legislation, policy developments and data requirements.
The selection procedure will therefore seek candidates with either a strong statistical/data profile or a strong legal/policy profile. The two profiles have a number of common requirements, while additional profile-specific criteria will be applied according to the candidate’s area of expertise.
The selection procedure will aim to establish a reserve list comprising up to three candidates for the Statistical/Data profile and up to three candidates for the Legal/Policy profile, for a maximum of six candidates in total. Candidates placed on the reserve list may be considered for secondment according to EIGE’s ongoing and future operational needs and subject to the applicable rules and availability of suitable secondment arrangements.
Job profile and duties
Under the supervision of the Head of the Research and Policy Support Unit and the relevant Team Leader, and working in close collaboration with colleagues across EIGE, the selected SNEs will enhance the Unit’s operational, analytical and research capacity in the area of gender-based violence and gender equality.
The posts require a very good understanding of gender equality and/or gender-based violence, strong analytical and research skills, the ability to work with EU and international policy frameworks, and excellent written and oral communication skills in English.
The duties will differ according to the selected profile as follows.
Profile 1 – Statistical/Data
The SNE appointed under the Statistical/Data profile will contribute primarily to the development, collection, validation, analysis and dissemination of statistical information and evidence on gender-based violence and gender equality.
The tasks may include:
Collect, process and analyse existing EU-wide data, including microdata, and produce statistics and analytical outputs in assigned research areas;
Contribute to the implementation and further development of EIGE’s EU-wide data collections, including administrative, survey and other relevant data sources;
Support the identification, assessment and use of relevant national, EU and international data sources;
Develop, review and improve statistical indicators relevant to measuring the incidence and prevalence of gender-based violence and progress in gender equality;
Contribute to the development of new indicators and methodologies responding to emerging policy and legislative needs;
Assess and validate the quality, comparability and consistency of statistical methods and data;
Identify limitations, gaps and inconsistencies in available data and propose approaches to improve data quality and comparability;
Produce comparative statistical analysis and data visualisations for research, policy and dissemination purposes;
Analyse microdata and conduct policy-relevant interpretative and comparative analysis;
Contribute to the analysis and use of administrative data from the justice sector and other relevant sectors in the context of the implementation of Directive (EU) 2024/1385;
Support the planning, implementation, quality assurance and final evaluation of statistical and research outputs delivered by EIGE contractors;
Develop and maintain statistical information exchange with relevant national, international and EU services;
Follow developments in statistical methodologies, data sources and data collection practices relating to gender-based violence and gender equality at national, European and international levels;
Contribute to the identification of data needs arising from EU legislation and policy developments;
Provide statistical and methodological input to EIGE research, reports, indicators, policy briefs and other outputs;
Contribute to multidisciplinary work with legal and policy colleagues, ensuring that statistical evidence is appropriately interpreted and translated into policy-relevant findings;
Contribute, as appropriate, to the monitoring and follow-up of relevant recommendations arising from the Istanbul Convention and GREVIO processes, particularly where statistical evidence and data are concerned.
Profile 2 – Legal/Policy
The SNE appointed under the Legal/Policy profile will contribute primarily to legal, policy, institutional and comparative analysis concerning gender-based violence, gender equality and related EU and international frameworks.
The tasks may include:
Analyse EU and national legal and policy frameworks relevant to gender-based violence and gender equality;
Contribute to the implementation of the provisions of Directive (EU) 2024/1385 falling within EIGE’s mandate;
Contribute to legal and policy analysis concerning the criminalisation of forms of violence against women, including rape, femicide and relevant forms of online gender-based violence;
Analyse the implementation of EU legislation and policies relevant to preventing and addressing violence against women and domestic violence;
Assess new and emerging EU legislation, including legislation in the areas of security, migration and asylum, from a gender equality and gender-based violence perspective;
Analyse the potential implications of EU and national legislation and policies for women experiencing gender-based violence;
Conduct comparative analysis of national legislation, policies, institutional arrangements and practices relating to gender-based violence and gender equality;
Identify and assess good practices, gaps and challenges in national responses to violence against women and domestic violence;
Contribute to the analysis and follow-up of GREVIO recommendations relevant to EIGE’s mandate, including the identification of priorities and areas for further action;
Contribute to legal and policy analysis concerning the implementation of the Istanbul Convention and other relevant international standards;
Analyse the interaction between legal, policy and institutional frameworks and the availability and use of administrative and statistical data on gender-based violence;
Contribute to the assessment of the implementation and impact of relevant EU legislation and policies;
Produce high-quality analytical, legal and policy-oriented reports, briefing notes and other outputs;
Support the development of policy recommendations based on evidence and comparative analysis;
Follow relevant legislative and policy developments at EU, national and international levels and identify emerging issues relevant to EIGE’s mandate;
Develop and maintain professional exchanges with relevant national administrations, EU institutions and agencies, international organisations and other stakeholders;
Contribute to multidisciplinary research and analytical work with statistical/data specialists and other EIGE colleagues.
Formal requirements & selection criteria
Formal requirements
To be considered eligible for selection, an applicant must meet the following formal requirements by the closing date of this call:
a university degree, or a level of formation which corresponds to completed university studies attested by a diploma and appropriate professional experience of at least one year when the normal period of university education is at least three years;
very good command of both spoken and written English, which is the predominant working language at the Agency, and a satisfactory knowledge of a second EU language;
entitlement to full rights as a European citizen or nationality of an EU candidate country or an EFTA country or a country with which the European Council has decided to open accession negotiations, and which has concluded a specific agreement with the Commission on staff secondments;
any obligations imposed by the national laws concerning military service.
The eligibility requirements are identical for both profiles.
Candidates who do not meet all formal eligibility requirements will not be considered further in the selection procedure.
Selection criteria
All eligible candidates will be assessed against the common selection criteria and, depending on the profile for which they apply, the relevant profile-specific criteria.
A. Common essential criteria – applicable to both profiles
Candidates must demonstrate:
At least four years of professional experience gained after the award of the relevant qualification and at a level corresponding to the responsibilities and tasks described in this vacancy;
Substantial professional experience in the field of gender-based violence, gender equality and/or social statistics;
Proven ability to analyse, interpret and critically assess relevant evidence and information;
Evident organisational skills, including the ability to manage priorities, work under pressure and meet tight deadlines;
Excellent interpersonal and problem-solving skills and the ability to work effectively with multiple stakeholders in a multicultural and multidisciplinary environment;
Demonstrated understanding of the policy and institutional context in which gender-based violence and gender equality are addressed.
B. Profile-specific essential criteria – Statistical/Data profile
In addition to the common essential criteria, candidates applying for the Statistical/Data profile must demonstrate:
Substantial professional experience in quantitative/statistical research and analysis relevant to gender-based violence and/or gender equality;
Proven experience in collecting, processing, analysing and interpreting quantitative data;
Proven experience with statistical methods and techniques appropriate to the candidate’s area of expertise;
Proven ability to assess data quality, comparability, reliability and limitations;
Experience working with official statistics and, where relevant, survey and/or administrative data;
Proven ability to develop, use or assess statistical indicators relevant to gender-based violence and/or gender equality;
Experience analysing microdata and/or conducting comparative statistical analysis;
Proven experience with data-analysis software, such as Excel, SPSS, Stata, R or equivalent tools;
Ability to translate statistical findings into clear, policy-relevant analytical conclusions.
C. Profile-specific essential criteria – Legal/Policy profile
In addition to the common essential criteria, candidates applying for the Legal/Policy profile must demonstrate:
Substantial professional experience in legal, policy, institutional and/or comparative analysis relevant to gender-based violence and/or gender equality;
Proven ability to analyse and interpret legal and policy frameworks and assess their practical implications;
Experience producing high-quality legal, analytical and/or policy-oriented reports;
Experience with EU and/or international legal and policy frameworks relevant to gender-based violence and/or gender equality;
Proven ability to conduct comparative analysis of legislation, policies, institutional arrangements and/or national practices;
Ability to assess the implementation and potential impact of legislation and policies from a gender equality and gender-based violence perspective;
Ability to identify gaps, challenges, good practices and areas for policy or legislative improvement;
Ability to interpret and use relevant official statistical and other evidence in support of legal and policy analysis.
Advantageous criteria
The following criteria will be considered advantageous for candidates under either profile, where relevant:
Knowledge of EU policies and legislation related to gender-based violence and/or gender equality;
Knowledge of Directive (EU) 2024/1385 on combating violence against women and domestic violence;
Knowledge of the Istanbul Convention and relevant GREVIO recommendations;
Experience working with EU institutions, agencies, national administrations or international organisations;
Experience working in a multidisciplinary and/or multicultural environment;
Experience establishing and maintaining professional networks and cooperation with national, European or international stakeholders;
Knowledge of emerging forms of gender-based violence, including technology-facilitated and online violence;
Experience working with justice-sector, migration, asylum, security or other administrative data and/or policy frameworks relevant to gender-based violence.
Selection procedure and application
Selection procedure
Only duly completed applications submitted electronically within the deadline will be taken into consideration.
All applications will first be examined to establish whether candidates meet the formal eligibility requirements set out in section 2.1.
A selection panel will be appointed by EIGE to conduct the selection procedure and to shortlist candidates for both profiles. The same selection panel will assess applications against the applicable common and profile-specific selection criteria, ensuring a consistent and transparent approach across the two profiles.
All applicants will be treated equally and assessed objectively against the selection criteria applicable to the profile for which they apply. Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the evidence provided in their application concerning their qualifications, professional experience, expertise and suitability for the duties of the relevant profile.
Following the assessment of admissible applications, the best-qualified candidates may be invited to an interview. Interviews will be conducted in English.
The selection procedure is intended to establish one reserve list covering both profiles, with:
up to 3 candidates for the Statistical/Data profile; and
up to 3 candidates for the Legal/Policy profile.
The reserve list may therefore contain up to 6 candidates in total.
Inclusion on the reserve list does not create an entitlement to secondment. Candidates on the reserve list may be considered for secondment where a suitable need arises, in accordance with EIGE’s applicable rules, the Agency’s priorities and operational requirements, and subject to the availability and agreement of the candidate’s employing administration.
The reserve list is intended to provide EIGE with access to appropriate expertise for ongoing and future needs in the field of gender-based violence, including needs arising from developments in EU legislation, implementation of Directive (EU) 2024/1385, the Istanbul Convention, data requirements, research activities and emerging policy priorities.
The chosen candidate(s), as appropriate, will be requested to provide:
A copy of an identity card, passport or other official document specifying citizenship;
A copy of the diploma certifying the required level of academic qualifications;
Documentary evidence of professional experience, clearly indicating starting and finishing dates.
Copies of the above-mentioned documents will be retained by the Agency in accordance with applicable data protection requirements.
If at any stage of the procedure it is established that information provided in the application has been knowingly falsified, the candidate shall be disqualified from the procedure.
The secondment shall be formalised through an exchange of letters between the Agency and the employer of the selected SNE.
Applications
Candidates should clearly indicate in their application whether they are applying for:
Profile 1 – Statistical/Data, or
Profile 2 – Legal/Policy.
Candidates should demonstrate explicitly how their qualifications and professional experience meet both the common essential criteria and the profile-specific essential criteria applicable to their chosen profile.
Where a candidate has substantial expertise relevant to both profiles, this may be indicated in the application. However, candidates should identify the profile under which they wish to be primarily assessed.
For applications to be valid, candidates must complete the EIGE application form, available only in English, and forward it electronically to eige.hr@eige.europa.eu. The subject title should include the vacancy reference number.
Applications may also be forwarded to EIGE on behalf of applicants by the Permanent Representations of the EU Member States.
Applicants are requested not to attach supporting documents at this stage, such as copies of identity cards, diplomas or evidence of previous professional experience. Only candidates shortlisted following the assessment and interview stage will be asked to provide documentary evidence for verification.
Applications will not be returned to candidates but will be retained by the Agency in accordance with its applicable data protection requirements.
Due to the large volume of applications, the Agency regrets that only candidates selected for the interview stage will be contacted.
Conditions of secondment
The purpose of the secondment is to provide the SNE with experience of the Agency's working methods and policies, to enable them to gain practical experience and understanding of the day-today work of its work and to give them the opportunity to work in a multicultural, multilingual environment. It also serves to enable staff of national administrations to put into practice the knowledge they have acquired in their studies, particularly in their respective areas of responsibility.
The SNE shall remain in the service of his/her employer throughout the period of secondment. The employer shall continue to pay the SNE's salary and maintain his/her administrative status and social rights, including social security and pension rights, throughout the secondment. The SNE shall be entitled to a daily subsistence allowance and a monthly subsistence allowance in accordance with Article 16 of EIGE Management Board Decision MB/2024/003 on the engagement and use of Seconded National Experts (SNEs) and National Experts in Professional Training (NEPTs).
The subsistence allowances are granted under the same conditions as the expatriation allowance for officials. The applicable amounts are based on the corresponding amounts for Brussels and take into account the correction coefficient applicable to Lithuania. The allowances are intended to cover living expenses at the place of secondment on a flat-rate basis and do not constitute remuneration paid by EIGE.
Candidates should ensure that their employer supports their candidacy and, if selected, is prepared to fulfil the obligations applicable to the secondment, including the continued payment of the SNE’s salary throughout the period of secondment.
The initial period of secondment will be for a minimum of one year. It may be extended in accordance with the applicable EIGE Rules on the engagement and use of Seconded National Experts (SNEs).
The place of secondment is EIGE’s office in Vilnius, Lithuania.
Independence & declarations of interest
The selected SNE will be required to enter into a commitment to act independently in the public interest and to make complete declarations of any direct or indirect interests that might be considered prejudicial to his or her independence.
Equal opportunities
The Agency applies a policy of equal opportunities in line with the formal requirements noted above.
Applications are accepted without distinction on any grounds of gender, race, colour, ethnic or social origin, genetic features, language, religion or belief, political or any other opinion, membership of a national minority, property, birth, disability, age or sexual orientation.
EIGE is committed to promote diversity and inclusion in its working environment and organisational culture. This includes Reasonable Accommodation for applicants with a disability3.
Appeal procedures
If a candidate considers that s/he has been adversely affected by a particular decision, s/he can lodge a complaint under Article 90(2) of the Staff Regulations of Officials of the European Union and Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union, by writing to The Director, European Institute for Gender Equality, Gedimino Prospektas 16, Vilnius, Lithuania LT01103.
The complaint must be lodged within three months. The time limit for initiating this type of procedure (see Staff Regulations as modified by Council Regulation No 723/2004 of 22nd March 2004 published in the Official Journal of the European Union L 124 of 27th April 2004) starts to run from the time the candidate is notified of the act adversely affecting her/him.
Candidates may also submit a complaint to the European Ombudsman concerning possible instances of maladministration by EIGE. Before submitting a complaint to the European Ombudsman, candidates should make use of the relevant administrative remedies available to them.
A complaint to the European Ombudsman does not suspend the applicable time limits for lodging an administrative complaint or bringing judicial proceedings.
Protection of personal data
As the body responsible for organising the competition, the EIGE ensures that applicants’ personal data are processed as required by Regulation (EU) 2018/1725 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2018 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data by the Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies and on the free movement of such data. This applies in particular to the confidentiality and security of such data.
Personal data shall thus be processed solely for the purpose of the selection procedure.
Lithuania and life in Vilnius
Lithuania is a Member State of the European Union and part of the Schengen Area. Its western coastline along the Baltic Sea is renowned for natural beauty, including sandy beaches, dunes and pine forests.
Vilnius, the capital, has a population of just over 550,000 and is situated on the banks of the river Neris. The city is known for its abundant green spaces and safe, family-friendly environment, offering excellent opportunities for outdoor and recreational activities. Vilnius combines rich cultural heritage, including Baroque, Gothic, Renaissance and classical architecture, with a vibrant contemporary life, making it attractive for both professionals and families. Its medieval old town is one of the largest preserved in Europe and has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1994.
Vilnius is the country’s main centre for politics, business, science, culture and innovation. It hosts a growing number of international conferences, professional networks and cultural events, offering a dynamic yet accessible urban environment. The city centre is compact, well-maintained and considered very safe.
Public transport is efficient, and most areas of the city are easily accessible. EIGE’s premises are located in the Europe House on Gedimino prospektas, the main thoroughfare, with convenient access to public transport, services, cultural venues and educational facilities.
Vilnius hosts several international and bilingual schools, , that provide high-quality education. The city is also home to a wide range of cultural and entertainment options, from museums, theatres and music venues to restaurants, cafés and sports facilities, providing a balanced lifestyle for both work and family life.
Further information is available on the websites of Go Vilnius and Invest Lithuania.

Staff from Public Administrations can work at EUSPA as ‘Seconded National Experts’ (SNEs). SNEs are seconded to the Agency while remaining in the service of their national employer and continuing to be paid their national salary by their employer. The Agency relies on National Experts in areas where advanced experience is available in National Administrations. About us (“We are”)

We are the Health Emergency Preparedness and Response Authority (DG HERA). DG HERA 's mission is to improve preparedness and response for serious cross border threats to health by ensuring access to medical countermeasures (MCM). It includes: • strengthening health security coordination involving all relevant actors during preparedness and crisis response times and bringing together the EU Member States, industry and relevant stakeholders in a common effort; • addressing vulnerabilities and strategic dependencies related to the development, production, procurement, stockpiling and distribution of MCM; • contributing to reinforcing the global health emergency response. DG HERA is responsible for the following tasks exercised in close cooperation with the Member States: • assessment of health threats and intelligence gathering relevant to MCM; • promoting advanced research and development of MCM and related technologies; • addressing market challenges and boosting the Union’s open strategic autonomy in MCM development and production; • swift procurement and distribution of MCM; • increasing stockpiling capacity of MCM; • strengthening knowledge and skills in preparedness and response related to MCM.

About the role (“We propose”)

The Deputy Head of DG HERA is seeking a motivated and dynamic colleague to provide support in his daily activities and contribute to the efficient functioning of the Deputy Head office. The position offers a varied and engaging working environment, with opportunities to take initiative and assume responsibility. The main responsibilities include managing the Deputy Head's agenda, organising meetings and missions (MIPS), monitoring and following up on incoming requests through Outlook, ARES and BASIS, as well as coordinating ISC matters within DG HERA. An important part of the role is also to support effective internal communication and ensure smooth coordination of incoming requests with the Heads of Unit and the administrative assistants of other HERA units.

Qualifications, experience and skills (“We look for”)

We are looking for a proactive, dependable and well-organised colleague who enjoys working as part of a team while also being able to work independently. The successful candidate will take responsibility for administrative workstreams and contribute to the effective management of the Deputy Head's office. The position requires a strong sense of responsibility, discretion and the ability to anticipate needs and priorities. Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, a positive and solution-oriented attitude, attention to detail and the ability to manage several tasks while adapting to changing priorities are essential. Previous experience in providing administrative support at senior management level would be considered an advantage. The ideal candidate should have excellent computer skills, particularly in MS Office and Excel, as well as a very good understanding of Commission administrative procedures and IT tools, notably ARES, BASIS, MIPS+ and Sysper. An excellent command of English is required, while knowledge of French would be considered an asset. As DG HERA is the DG responsible for ensuring preparedness and response to health crises, the recruited colleague will be expected to demonstrate flexibility in terms of tasks and working hours. Occasional atypical working hours (including evenings and weekends) may be required, particularly in times of crisis.

How to express your interest?

You should send your documents in a single pdf in the following order:

1. your CV

2. completed application form.

Please send these documents by the publication deadline to HERA-HR-CORRESPONDENTec [dot] europa [dot] eu (HERA-HR-CORRESPONDENT[at]ec[dot]europa[dot]eu) indicating the selection reference DG HERA/COM/2026/1952 in the subject.

No applications will be accepted after the publication deadline.

MAKE A DIFFERENCE  - JOIN THE EUROPEAN COMMISSION

Do you want to help shape the future of the European Union? Make the planet greener,
promote a fairer society, or support businesses and innovation across the EU? Then come and
work for the European Commission where you can really make a difference!

Commission staff are a diverse group of people, who are motivated to help make Europe – and
the world – a better place. They come from the 27 Member States of the European Union.
Different nationalities, backgrounds, languages and cultures make the Commission a vibrant and
inclusive place to work.

WE OFFER GREAT JOBS AND GREAT WORKING CONDITIONS:

  •  Interesting and challenging jobs with plenty of opportunities for training and acquiring
  new skills and competencies throughout your whole career
  •  Opportunities to move between different policy areas throughout your career
  •  A package of flexible working conditions including the possibility of teleworking – we
  care about your work-life balance
  •  A competitive financial package, including comprehensive healthcare, accident and
  pension schemes
  •  A multilingual, multicultural workplace where personal and career development are
  strongly promoted
  •  Multilingual schools for your children

We recruit from a wide range of backgrounds and actively promote diversity and
inclusion:

We do not only recruit political scientists and lawyers but are also looking for all kinds of
profiles, including scientists, linguists, IT experts, data analysts and economists, as well as drivers
and engineers.

We are committed to equal opportunities and to fostering a rich, diverse and inclusive working
environment. We aim for our workforce to be representative of European society and strongly
welcome applications from all qualified candidates. We actively seek to create a workplace where
each staff member feels valued and respected, can give their best and can develop to their full
potential.

  JUST/COM/2026/2175

To promote diversity and establish a geographically balanced pool of candidates, we strongly
encourage applicants from Member States which are currently underrepresented in the European

Malta, Poland, Slovakia and Sweden1. Recruitment will however remain strictly based on the

State.

For more information ec.europa.eu/work-with-us

  STAFF RECRUITED ON CONTRACTS

In addition to permanent officials, the European Commission offers non-permanent positions.
There are two categories of non-permanent staff:
  •  temporary agents are recruited to fill vacant positions for a set amount of time or
  to perform highly specialised tasks.
  •  contract agents may provide additional capacity in specialised fields where an
  insufficient number of officials is available or carry out a number of administrative or
  manual tasks. They are generally recruited for fixed-term contracts (maximum 6 years in
  any EU Institution), but in some cases they can be offered contracts for an indefinite

WE ARE

Unit JUST.C3 is responsible for the protection of personal data as a fundamental right in the EU.
The EU data protection rules  – the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the Data
Protection Law Enforcement Directive - are key EU achievements. Ensuring that the new legislation
delivers for people living in the EU is therefore a priority objective for the Commission and our unit
in particular. To this end, we monitor the compliance of national legislation,  integrate data
protection into all relevant EU policy initiatives, and actively engage with all actors, in particular
data protection authorities, businesses and civil society. With a wide range of EU policies
increasingly involving the processing of personal data, we work closely with a wide range of
Commission services in areas such as artificial intelligence and the related data strategy, health,
financial services, mobility and law enforcement, in order to ensure that the fundamental right to
the protection of personal data is duly respected.

WE PROPOSE

We offer a position for a motivated and eager to learn unit secretary in a dynamic work
environment. The new colleague will be an integral part of the team and will work in close
cooperation with the head of unit, all members of the unit and other colleagues in the Directorate-

services and stakeholders.

The position will consist of a wide variety of tasks contributing to the smooth running of the unit by

handling unit mail, assisting in handling briefings, support in interaction with external stakeholders,
including other EU bodies, preparing business trips , organising meetings (on -line or physical), and
assisting in coordinating and handling citizen’s complaints, access to documents request, petitions
and other similar requests. S/he will ensure the administrative support to colleagues in handling
consultations on legal acts to be adopted by the Commis sion (interservice-consultations).

Generation 2004 is seeking to recruit one full-time Secretary (FG II), based in
Brussels.
The purpose of this role is to provide reliable and efficient administrative, logistical

statutory meetings, working groups and hybrid webinars, including the circulation of

briefings, communication and any other logistical assistance related to the activities

of Generation 2004; and serving as a regular operational point of contact, liaising
with Commission services, members and external partners.

Qualifications, experience and skills

 About us (“We are”):

 The Directorate General for Internal Market, Industry, Entrepreneurship and SMEs
 is working to uphold and manage the Single Market for goods and services and to
 strengthen its governance. Its work helps ensure an open, seamless and resilient
 internal market, which is one of the cornerstones of European integration.

 The DG supports the competitiveness, growth and resilience of the EU economy. It
 focuses on strengthening the leadership of European industries across different
 industrial ecosystems, by leveraging the power of the Single Market and addressing
 strategic dependencies in our supply chains. In addition, it implements policies that
 sustain entrepreneurship and growth, in particular to the benefit of small and
 medium sized enterprises (SMEs), including facilitating access to funding and to
 global markets for EU companies.

 The DG also leads efforts on digitalisation and decarbonisation of European industry
 and SMEs. It contributes to the objective of turning the EU into a greener, more
 digital and more resilient economy.

 DG GROW.B4 is the central unit for stakeholder engagement, supporting the
 implementation of the competitiveness and simplification agenda on the ground.
 We coordinate the Industrial Forum and its activities, oversight of industrial alliances,
 clusters and business support networks.

We are responsible for policy coordination and oversight of the Enterprise Europe
Network, European Cluster Collaboration Platform, Euroclusters, and Erasmus for
Young  Entrepreneurs  programmes,  together  with  other  initiatives.
Through our event organisation and our networks, we help the Commission to reach
out to businesses, clusters, business support organisations and other stakeholders
to explain EU policies and get their feedback and business intelligence.
This helps us shape industrial and cluster policy on the ground through collaboration
and competition, and provide practical business support including, partnership and
training to help companies innovate and grow in the Single Market and beyond,
including supporting the integration of businesses from accession countries.
About the role (“We propose”):

We offer an interesting position with a varied range of tasks for an experienced
secretary/administrative assistant. This is an opportunity to join a dynamic team
and play an important role in ensuring the smooth running of the unit’s daily work.

The position will involve managing the functional mailboxes, documents and
correspondence, preparation of missions, organisation and logistics of meetings,
expert groups and conferences, various operational tasks such as support to
financial management, monitoring deadlines and supporting a positive and
collegial team environment.

The post offers a varied day-to-day work environment, combining internal
coordination, contact with stakeholders and support to high-visibility meetings and
events. In this role, the selected candidate will contribute directly to work that
supports European business and SMEs and helps improve the conditions for
companies to innovate and grow.

The selected candidate will work in a close cooperation with another administrative
assistant in the unit.

Qualifications, experience and skills (“We look for”):

We are looking for a motivated, proactive and reliable colleague who has high
organisational and communication skills and pays attention to details. The position
requires team spirit, flexibility and adaptability to fast-changing priorities. We seek a
candidate with an ability to manage multiple tasks, prioritise effectively and organise
their work independently.

The candidate would be expected to have good computer skills (Word, Excel,
Outlook, Teams) and willingness to learn and develop new technical skills.

Prior experience of working in the EU institutions would be an asset. Very good
knowledge of English is essential, and French would be an asset. Knowledge of
other EU languages would be an advantage.

 1. your CV  2.  completed  application  form.

postings.description:
About us

The European Commission’s Directorate-General International Partnerships (DG INTPA) is responsible for the elaboration of EU development and international cooperation policies and strategies as well as the implementation of relevant EU external action funding instruments in partner countries in Sub-Saharan Africa, Asia - Pacific as well as in the Americas.

Within the thematic directorate INTPA.G: ‘Human Development, Migration, Governance and Peace’, unit INTPA.G6 'Migration and Forced displacement', is in charge of migration, mobility and forced displacement. The mandate of the unit is based on three main axes:

- The formulation of EU policies and operational approaches in the areas of migration, mobility and forced displacement, and active participation in political dialogue with internal as well as external stakeholders on these issues. An important aspect of this work concerns coordination and cooperation with the other EU services, EU Member States, with external actors and interlocutors as well as with Partner countries.
- Providing thematic guidance for colleagues in both DG INTPA and in EU delegations on how to address migration and forced displacement challenges and opportunities through international cooperation. Activities include drafting of orientation and guidance material, organising training sessions, providing tailor-made support on demand, in coordination with geographical units, as well as contributing to quality processes for programmes and projects managed by geographical directorates of DG INTPA.
- Operational and financial management of the Migration and Forced Displacement component of the thematic programme NDICI-Global Europe / Global Challenges.

The unit is organised into two sections; i) Migration and Mobility and ii) Asylum and Forced displacement.

About the role

Unit INTPA.G6 is seeking to hire one secretary to the Unit.

In this position, you will have a key role in contributing to the successful implementation of the unit’s mission through providing assistance and administrative support to the Head of Unit as well as to the other members of the Unit

The main tasks include:

- Administrative and practical assistance to the head of unit in the overall management of the unit’s tasks;
- Manage and supervise all incoming and outgoing communication and correspondence, including parliamentary questions, interservice consultations, access to documents requests, citizens questions, ensuring correct attribution and respect of deadlines, as well as proper archiving;
- Ensuring access to and information about administrative issues, processes and procedures for the Unit staff;
- Ensure logistical and administrative support in the organisation of meetings and events, including the handling of personal data of external participants, the escorting of external participants to and from the meeting room, the support for the establishment of online connections;
- Prepare missions by arranging travel for all members of the unit and monitoring of the unit’s mission budget;
- Assist members of the unit in the administrative and contractual tasks related to contract preparation and implementation;
- Provide assistance in the management of Annual Action Plans: launch of ISC in Decide and follow-up (planning, quality support meetings, decision and legiswrite, agreement of cabinet).
- E-Domec Focal Point: Contribute to archiving correspondence (including registering in ARES) and to storing, reproducing, circulating and/or retrieving documents.
- Data Protection Focal Point within unit: redact all personal data before disseminating through the EASE tool (Access to documents).

We offer a very pleasant work environment with positive and motivated colleagues and many opportunities for personal development.

Qualifications, experience and skills

We are looking for:

- A motivated, dynamic and flexible colleague who enjoys teamwork and has a strong sense of responsibility and organisation.
- The position requires very good communication and organisational skills, as well as good IT skills.
- The ideal candidate should have a very good command of English and French.

How to express your interest?

- Your CV 2. Completed application form

About us (“We are”)

Unit CNECT.02 is the Communication unit of the Directorate-General for
Communications Networks, Content and Technology (DG CNECT). We are a
dynamic and visible horizontal unit, responsible for communicating the European
Commission’s vision for Europe’s digital transformation to the outside world.

As digital technology changes people’s lives, we communicate externally on the vast
work of the DG from ground-breaking regulation in areas such as Artificial
Intelligence, over platforms to funding cutting-edge research and deployment,
including some of the world’s fastest supercomputers. We cooperate closely with
the interinstitutional unit in DG CNECT and report directly to the Director-General.

About the role (“We propose”)

A varied and interesting post as secretary to the Head of Unit (HoU) and the unit,
combining administrative support with broader organisational and planning tasks,
including communication overviews and document handling.

You will contribute to the efficient functioning of the unit by facilitating the
organisation of work, coordinating administrative procedures and processes,
helping us deliver timely, quality outputs and achieving our objectives.

Your tasks would include:

  •  providing administrative and logistical support to the HoU and colleagues in
  the unit, keeping agenda, preparing important events, organising and
  coordinating meetings as well as welcoming visitors;
  •  supporting our organisation and planning of work, keeping track of the
  agenda, and organising meetings; keeping track of the unit’s deliveries,
  distributing and coordinating our deliverables through Outlook (including our
  functional mailboxes), Teams, Ares and the briefing IT tool “Basis”;
  •  coordinating the unit’s input to corporate planning and reporting as regards
  strategy, missions, risks assessments etc.;
  •  coordinating the unit’s storage, deletion, registration and circulation of
  documents;
  •  keeping our intranet webpages updated with relevant qualitative content;
  •  preparing and sharing documents for collaborative working in Teams as well
  as occasionally preparing notes, minutes and routine correspondence;
  •  assisting mission registration in MIPS+ and presence registrations in Sysper;
  •  supporting our financial assistant in contract preparations and monitoring.

This is a fun and interesting position that offers the possibility to be part of a close-
knit and lively unit which communicates on all DG CNECT’s legislative and policy
initiatives as well as research and implementing results to the media and the general
public. You will interact with our four teams (web, press, outreach and audiovisual),
working together to deliver communication products across multiple channels.

Qualifications, experience and skills (“We look for”)

A collaborative team player wanting to work in a young and dynamic team.

Are you responsible, well organised and proactive? Can you provide reliable
secretarial and administrative support? Are you positive and ready to take on new
challenges? Do you also have an interest in financial matters? If so, this job is for
you!

Good planning skills and attention to priorities, deadlines and details are essential.
You should have good IT skills and experience with administrative functions.
Knowledge of the main Commission applications, processes and procedures as well
as prior knowledge and understanding of digital policies would be an asset.

Good communication skills and a strong command of English are required. Good
knowledge of French would be an asset.

02@ec.europa.eu indicating the selection reference CNECT/COM/2026/2144 in the

About us (“We are”)

Unit A.3 deals with various topics concerning transparency and ethics.

It provides advice on the application of the ethical rules for the Members of the
College (Code of Conduct for the Members of the European Commission) as well
as on issues related to patronage (moral support) of events by Commissioners.
The unit handles files concerning post mandate activities of former Members and
provides secretarial support to the Commission’s Independent Ethical Committee.
It coordinates with DG HR on the rights and ethical obligations of staff, as well as
on the disciplinary aspects of the Staff Regulations, and it contributes to the
handling of other ethics-related institutional issues, including those related to the
Protocol on Privileges and Immunities of the European Union.

The unit manages the Transparency Register and is responsible for designing and
implementing the Commission's policy on transparency concerning interest
representation, in particular with regard to the implementation of the relevant
Interinstitutional Agreement and the Commission's associated framework,
including the policy on publication of meetings with interest representatives. It
participates on behalf of the Commission in the tri-institutional Secretariat of the
Transparency Register (Parliament – Council – Commission).

Unit A.3 is furthermore in charge of the Commission’s relations with the European
Ombudsman, including the coordination of the handling of the Ombudsman’s
inquiries concerning the Commission. In relation to the Commission’s Code of
Good Administrative Behaviour, the unit handles the complaint procedure
established by this Code.

The unit is also in charge of relations with the European Anti-Fraud Office (OLAF),
coordinates anti-fraud policy issues, and handles information that the Commission
receives from OLAF on internal investigations. As regards relations with the
European Public Prosecutor’s Office, the unit oversees the general framework for
the cooperation between the Commission and the EPPO, and within the
Commission, in relation to the EPPO’s investigations into criminal offences
affecting the Commission. It is currently co-leading the ongoing review of the Anti-
Fraud Architecture.

Finally, the unit is responsible for the Commission rules on the Commission’s
participation in private-law bodies.
About the role (“We propose”)

We are offering an interesting and diverse post in the unit's secretariat, consisting
of performing a variety of general secretarial tasks and assume administrative
responsibilities in order to keep the office running smoothly. The tasks will include
providing administrative support to the Head and Deputy Head of Unit, including in
personnel matters, as well as to desk officers on files.

The secretary will contribute to the work of the secretariat monitoring incoming
tasks and correspondence in Ares, Decide, and the functional mailboxes of the
Unit and ensuring assignments according to the instructions given, monitoring the
respect of deadlines, and preparing and monitoring internal procedures.
Furthermore, the secretariat is processing the unit's contributions to replies to
interservice consultations, parliamentary questions, correspondence etc and is
also ensuring proper archiving and record management. The tasks will also
include the organisation of meetings, requesting translations and ensuring the
availability of office supplies. Furthermore, the secretary will assist in the
monitoring and updating of information on websites related to the unit's activities,

According to the needs, the secretary may be asked to provide administrative
assistance to the Transparency Register team of the unit that is also working as a
part of the interinstitutional Transparency Register Secretariat.

The work will include the handling of sensitive and confidential information for
which the respect of the professional secrecy is imperative.

Qualifications, experience and skills (“We look for”)

We are looking for a proactive colleague with a relevant administrative background,
IT-skills as well as mail and document management skills. Experience from similar
administrative support functions in the Commission and experience with Ares,
Decide, Eurolook, Sysper, MIPS+ (Missions Integrated Processing System),
Webdor, POETRY and other Commission IT systems will be a clear advantage.

The candidate should be able to work autonomously as well as in a team and should
be able to handle sensitive and confidential information in full respect of the
obligation of professional secrecy.

The candidate should have very good English and French competences, both orally
and in writing, and further language skills would be an advantage. As the position
involves a wide variety of contacts, including in the Cabinets, the person should be
at ease with high-level contacts and be able to handle such contacts appropriately.

How to express your interest?

You should send your documents in a single pdf in the following order:
 1. your CV
2. the completed application form.
Please send these documents by the publication deadline to
SG-UNITE-A-3@ec.europa.eu
indicating the selection reference SG/COM/2026/1879 in the subject.

No applications will be accepted after the publication deadline.

Eligibility
For eligibility please consult this page with all the information needed.

postings.title: Secretary to the Head of Representation
postings.description:
WE ARE

The Directorate-General of Communication in Member States oversees services targeting national
audiences. This includes the European Commission Representations in the Member States. The
Representation of the European Commission in Malta has the mandate to:
• Support the President and the whole Commission in their interaction with Malta.
• Promote permanent political dialogue with the national, regional and local authorities,
parliaments, social partners, other stakeholders, academia and civil society. The
Representation prepares and supports visits by Members of the College and by senior
officials of the Commission and, as appropriate, of the European External Action Service.
• Act as the Commission’s voice in Malta and communicate about the EU to media and on
social media, maintaining direct contacts with national, regional and local media and
offering press and media services to them.
• Engage with citizens, academia, civil society, social partners and other stakeholders, and
organise outreach activities about EU priorities policies, programmes and projects on the
ground.
• Provide country knowledge, analysis and advice on the political, economic and social
developments in Malta to the President and the Commission with a view to informing EU
policy making and political communication.

WE PROPOSE

The Representation in Valletta is seeking to hire a dedicated Contract Agent FGII to fill the role of
Secretary to the Head of Representation and join a dynamic multicultural team. This crucial
position is designed to ensure the seamless operation of the Representation through a variety of
tasks. The successful candidate will provide support to and manage the agenda of the Head of
Representation, take care of general administrative assignments, and contribute to smooth internal
and external communications for the visibility of the Representation. Responsibilities include
organising work trips, agendas and meetings, dealing with protocol teams for high-level visits,
engaging with a host of external stakeholders, helping prepare briefs and meetings and assisting in
the coordination of Representation’s activities, managing the functional mailboxes of the
Representation and assisting with document management, human resources and contract
management as needed.

WE LOOK FOR

We are looking for a skilled and proactive individual to fill the role of Secretary to the Head of
Representation.
The ideal profile for the job includes:
• Experience: At least 3 years of job-related experience in operational and administrative
support and resources, along with a solid understanding of information and document
management. Additional experience in such fields will be considered an advantage.
• Languages: Proficiency in Maltese (C2) and English (C1).
• Skills: Strong capabilities in IT tools for office automation (Excel, Outlook, Word) and IT
systems specific to the European Commission.
• Competencies: A candidate who excels in multi-tasking, organising, analysing and problem-
solving, possesses good communication skills, resilience in the day-to-day work. Plus, the
ability to work autonomously and proactively. A service-oriented colleague who knows how
to prioritise tasks and collaborate with a team.
• A general knowledge of the European Commission. Additional knowledge of EU policies will
be considered an advantage.

HOW TO EXPRESS YOUR INTEREST?

With a view to guaranteeing equal access to all, the Commission recruits from an open database of
spontaneous applications. The present call for interests aims at helping the recruiters to identify
potentially interested candidates within this database.
In practice, to express your interest, please follow the subsequent two steps:
1. If you are not registered yet in the open EPSO database, please do so at the following
address: CAST Permanent. Please select under selection procedures for contract agent the
CAST permanent profile that best suits your education and experience.
2. You should send your documents in a single pdf in the following order:
1. your CV 2. completed application form.

postings.domain: Cybersecurity, EU’s internal and external security
postings.description:
This selection procedure is intended to establish a reserve list of successful candidates. It is envisaged to start using the reserve list in Q4 of 2026/Q1 of 2027.

Europol retains the right to make use of the reserve list to select candidates for similar posts within the organisation, should business needs require so.

1. Organisational context

Organisational setting:
The post of Senior Specialist – Head of Team – Cybercrime Investigations Support is located in in one of the teams within the European Cybercrime Centre (EC3), Operations Directorate.

The Operations Directorate deals with the core business of Europol, improving the effectiveness and cooperation of the competent authorities in the Member States (MS) in preventing and combating serious and organised crime as well as terrorism affecting the MS. This requires close cooperation with the Liaison Bureaux at Europol and via them with the Operational Teams in the MS.

Europol delivers a number of products and services to national law enforcement agencies to support them in their fight against international serious and organised crime, as well as terrorism.

The Operations Directorate hosts six distinct Departments: Operational and Analysis Centre (OAC), European Serious Organised Crime Centre (ESOCC), European Cyber Crime Centre(EC3), European Counter Terrorism Centre, European Financial and Economic Crime Centre (EFECC) and European Centre Against Migrant Smuggling (ECAMS).

EC3 serves as the centre for the MS fight against cybercrime in the European Union, delivering operational and investigative support on complex cybercrime investigations.

EC3 also provides support to the EU institutions and MS in building operational and analytical capacity for investigations and cooperation with external partners. EC3 is the collective voice of European cybercrime investigators across law enforcement and the knowledge hub of law enforcement on how to tackle cybercrime.

The Centre comprises of three Units, each with their own area of responsibility.
The EC3 Operations Unit is responsible for delivering the operational services to MS of EU and other partners with whom Europol has operational agreements. The Unit consist of five teams: AP Cyborg (cyber-dependent crime), AP Terminal (payment fraud and on-line fraud schemes), AP Twins (child sexual exploitation), AP Dark Web (criminal use of anonymization services) and the J-CAT coordination team (operational support to the Joint Cybercrime Action Taskforce).

The EC3 Expertise & Stakeholder Management Unit is responsible for the coordination and deconfliction of various cases within the mentioned crime areas, enriching related data sets, delivering analytical support and advising and participating in operational actions.

The Digital Support Unit is assisting EC3 Operations and provides horizontal support to other Operations Centres of Europol by delivering intelligence products, technical and forensic support, decryption and cryptocurrency tracing services and facilitating technical assistance in handling large datasets through three dedicated teams: Cyber Intelligence Team (CIT), Forensics Team (FT) and Cryptocurrency Team.

Purpose of the post:
The jobholder will be responsible for leading, managing and coordinating the activities of one of the teams within EC3 in order to support the Member States and other Europol’s partners in the fight against cyber dependent and cyber enabled crimes.

There are several Head of Team vacancies coming up within the next two years, namely The Head of Team JCAT, the Head of Team AP Terminal and the Head of Team Digital Forensics Team.

Reporting lines:
The incumbent reports to the Head of EC3 Operations Unit or Head of EC3 Digital Support Unit.

2. Functions and duties

The incumbent carries out the following main functions and duties:

General Head of Team responsibilities

- Coordinate the work of a group of individuals by effective and efficient planning, prioritisation, and scheduling of tasks and responsibilities;
- Monitor progress of work in line with key performance indicators; ensure work being produced is of high quality and meets business needs; apply corrective measures where needed;
- Define and supervise the accurate and timely execution of processes and procedures to ensure adherence to corporate policies, fundamental rights, standards and data protection regulations;
- Set clear expectations and objectives and direct work towards a common goal;
- Identify, address and propose resolutions to issues affecting the team;
- Provide constructive feedback, guidance and support and coach team members;
- Encourage continuous learning and development of team members;
- Create an open, honest and inclusive team culture with respect for diversity, where team members are encouraged to perform at their best.

Specific responsibilities

- Support the development and the implementation of the Europol strategy in the field of responsibility;
- Participate in European or international projects, where Europol participates as a member or as the leading agency;
- Oversee the support of cybercriminal operations and investigations in accordance with Europol’s mandate;
- Safeguard development and maintenance of expertise in the area of responsibility, through research, study and liaison with relevant agencies and experts;
- Facilitate and steer the production of reports and documents in the area of competence;
- Ensure efficient and effective operational, technical, forensic, or financial support to Member States on the spot and at Europol Headquarters;
- Establish close contacts with the Member States and Third Parties’ Liaison Officers to encourage and support operational activities in the field of responsibility;
- Perform any other duties in the area of competence as assigned by the line management.

3. Requirements - Eligibility criteria

a. Candidates must

- Be a member of a competent authority within the meaning of the Article 2(a) of the Europol Regulation and enjoy full rights as a citizen of a Member State;
- Have fulfilled any obligations imposed by the applicable laws on military service;
- Produce appropriate character references as to his or her suitability for the performance of the duties;
- Be physically fit to perform the duties pertaining to the post as further specified in Article 13 of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (CEOS);
- Produce evidence of a thorough knowledge of one of the languages of the Union and a satisfactory knowledge of another language of the Union to the extent necessary for the performance of the duties.

b. Candidates must have

- A level of education which corresponds to completed university studies attested by a diploma when the normal period of university education is four years or more;

OR

- A level of education which corresponds to completed university studies attested by a diploma and appropriate professional experience of at least one year when the normal period of university education is at least three years;

OR

- Professional training of an equivalent level in a relevant area (e.g. Police Officer’s School) and after having completed the training, at least the number of years of relevant professional experience as indicated below:

Duration of professional training Additional professional experience required for equivalency
More than 6 months and up to 1 year 4 years
More than 1 year and up to 2 years 3 years
More than 2 years and up to 3 years 2 years
More than 3 years 1 year

- In addition to the above at least 9 years of total professional work experience gained after the award of the diploma.

4. Requirements - Selection criteria

a. Professional experience
Essential:

- Preferably at least 5 years of experience working in a cybercrime unit in the one of the EU MS or at international LEA;
- Preferably at least 3 years of experience managing staff supporting operational activities and/or conducting criminal investigations;
- Experience in producing intelligence reports;
- Experience in coordinating investigations or support activities in one or more of the following areas of expertise:
- Cybercrime investigations;
- Cyber (threat) intelligence;
- Digital forensics;
- Payment frauds;
- Darkweb investigations.

- Experience with applying big dataset analysis and AI techniques within criminal investigations.

Desirable:

- Extensive experience in international Law Enforcement cooperation in the cybercriminal domain;
- Experience in working with private entities within the cybersecurity landscape;

b. Professional knowledge
Essential:

- Sound knowledge of current threat actors, their modus operandi and emerging trends in cybercrime, payment fraud, dark web activities, and relevant forensic techniques;
- Knowledge of the law-enforcement environment and intelligence practices in general and of the field of responsibility in particular (cybercrime, payment fraud, darkweb and/or digital forensics);
- Knowledge of cybersecurity matters, with a focus on cyber threat intelligence (CTI), including relevant private-sector stakeholders within the cybersecurity landscape;
- Knowledge of AI-driven solutions relevant to cybersecurity and cybercrime landscape;
- Knowledge of methods and techniques applied in the full cycle of cybercrime investigations;
- Knowledge of the EU legal framework in general and in the area of law enforcement cooperation in particular;
- Knowledge on international legal instruments in the area of cybercrime.

c. General competencies
Essential:
Communicating:

- Excellent communication skills in English, both orally and in writing;
- Excellent presentation skills;
- Ability to draft clear and concise documents on complex matters for various
Audiences;

Analysing & problem solving:

- Structured approach to work aimed at getting results;
- Excellent analytical and critical thinking skills;
- Competent user of Microsoft Office applications (MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook) and the internet.

Delivering quality and results:

- High degree of commitment and flexibility.
- High level of customer and service-orientation.

Prioritising & organising:

- Excellent organizational skills including the ability to plan own workload, establish clear priorities and exercise initiative;
- Ability to manage projects and familiarity with project management terminology and methodology.

Resilience:

- Strong ability to work well both independently and in a team;
- Very good interpersonal skills, including the ability to effectively liaise with other departments, groups and teams as well as with external partners;
- Ability to remain effective under a heavy workload and demonstrate resistance to stress.

Living diversity:

- Ability to establish and maintain effective working relations with co-workers in an international and multi-disciplinary work environment.

Advising:

- Ability to synthesise various data into a coherent and relevant whole, transforming it into a valuable and correct conclusion;
- Building constructive relationships with clients and team members, adequately identifying and managing their needs and expectations, and giving well-grounded advice.

Team supervision:

- Ability to manage a diverse team including the ability to motivate staff, effectively plan and monitor the work of other staff members and to provide guidance.

d. Additional conditions:
Fulfil the condition stipulated in Article 5 of the Decision of the Executive Director on the Duration of contracts of employment for Temporary Agents, on the start date of the possible contract of employment which may be offered.

5. Selection procedure

All applications for Temporary Agent posts must be submitted through the online recruitment system accessible via Europol’s website. For further information, please consult the Europol Recruitment Guidelines.

The Authority Authorised to Conclude Contracts of Employment (AACC) sets up a Selection Committee, composed of at least three members, consisting of one chair and at least one member from the administration and one member designated by the Staff Committee.

For restricted posts (including restricted - Annex II posts), the AACC designates up to two additional members of the Selection Committee if so requested by the Chairperson of the Management Board. The additional members shall consist of a representative of the Presidency of the Council of the European Union or one representative of the Presidency and one representative of another Member State.

The selection criteria, set out in this Vacancy Notice, will be assessed by the Selection Committee throughout the different stages of the selection procedure. Before the start of the selection procedure, the Selection Committee will decide which selection criteria will be used at each stage of the selection procedure. Certain selection criteria will be assessed only for shortlisted candidates during a written test and/or a competency-based interview.

The Selection Committee will assess the applications received in order to make an initial selection of those candidates meeting all eligibility criteria and matching best the selection criteria (suitability).

In case of candidates shortlisted for restricted posts (including restricted - Annex II posts), who had indicated membership of a competent authority in one of the Member States, Europol will seek confirmation from the relevant Europol National Unit to ensure that those candidates indeed belong to a competent authority.

The minimum pass-mark for being shortlisted, i.e. invited to participate in a post-related selection procedure, consisting of a written test and a competency-based interview, is established as 60% of the total maximum score.

The Selection Committee will shortlist the 12 highest scoring candidates. All candidates having a score equal to the 12th highest scoring candidate will be invited to take part in the selection procedure. At shortlisting stage, the Selection Committee will establish the pass-mark for the selection procedure.

It is intended for the selection procedure to be conducted remotely. Should the Selection Committee consider it necessary to conduct the selection procedure on-site at Europol in the interest of the proceedings, and subject to budget availability, the candidates invited to participate in the selection procedure will be informed accordingly.

After the selection procedure has taken place, the Selection Committee will establish a list of successful candidates, i.e. those scoring above the pre-defined pass-mark, which is shared with the AACC, for establishment of a Reserve list. A Reserve list is valid for 24 months.

Candidates who participated in the interview will be informed of the outcome, i.e. whether they have been successful or not.
The Selection Committee’s work and deliberations are confidential. It is forbidden for candidates to make direct or indirect contact with the members of the Selection Committee or for anyone to do so on their behalf.

All enquiries related to a selection procedure should be addressed to the Europol HR Operational Support Team at the following email address: C2-12europol [dot] europa [dot] eu (C2-12[at]europol[dot]europa[dot]eu). Detailed information on the selection procedure- including enquiries, measures of redress and their applicable deadlines is available in the Europol Recruitment Guidelines, which can be found on Europol’s website www.europol.europa.eu.

6. Compensation and benefits
Scale: AD8
The gross basic monthly salary is EUR 8,911.48 (step 1) or EUR 9,285.95 (step 2).

The step in grade is determined on the basis of professional experience gained after the education required for the post and in line with applicable implementing rules.

Staff pay EU tax at source but salaries are exempt from national taxes. Compulsory deductions are made for health insurance, pension and unemployment insurance.

Subject to the applicable conditions being met, as defined in the EU Staff Regulations (EUSR)/CEOS and further specified in the case law of the Court of Justice of the European Union, allowances such as expatriation allowance (16% of basic gross salary) or foreign residence allowance (4% of basic gross salary), household allowance, dependent child and / or education allowance may be granted.

Staff enjoy worldwide insurance coverage by the Joint Sickness Insurance Scheme (JSIS) and are insured against sickness, the risk of occupational disease and accident.

Europol offers flexible working arrangements, a comprehensive provision for annual leave as well as parental leave supporting a healthy work-life balance.

Indicative net salary sample calculation AD8/1:
