postings.title: SNE - Communications Officer
postings.description:
Description of the Agency's tasks

ECHA is the driving force among regulatory authorities in implementing the EU's ground-breaking chemicals legislation for the benefit of human health and the environment as well as for innovation and competitiveness. ECHA helps companies to comply with the legislation, promotes the safe use of chemicals, provides information on chemicals and addresses chemicals of concern. You will find more information on ECHA and the different Regulations on ECHA website at: http://www.echa.europa.eu

General requirements

Candidates for secondment must:

• Have current employment in the national, regional or local public sector or international civil service. Alternatively candidates may be employed in a non-profit or voluntary sector;

• Hold a university degree in a field relevant to the areas of work described in this call;

• Be a national of an EU or EFTA Member State or a candidate country as decided by the Council;

• Be able to communicate in written and spoken English as this is the working language of ECHA.

Secondment

The secondment will be subject to an exchange of letters between the Head of People and Development of ECHA and the applicant’s employer. The duration of the first secondment is a maximum of one year. This period may be renewed for a maximum of three additional years.

Seconded National Experts remain in the service of their employer throughout the period of their secondment. The sending organisation must continue remunerating the SNE, who will thus benefit from social security coverage. During their secondment, SNEs will receive subsistence allowances and reimbursement of expenses as set out in the “Rules on the secondment of national experts to the European Chemicals Agency” (Decision ED-0050).

The SNE Rules

Profile

Seconded National Expert – Communications Officer; ref.: ECHA/SNE/2026/002

Our ideal candidate is a communications professional with experience gained working in a national authority, national ministry, European institution or European agency. Comfortable in a changing environment, you are adaptable, resilient and have good interpersonal and networking skills. You are curious about developments in your field and communications more broadly.

The Unit is responsible for ECHA’s communications activities, including press relations, external and internal communications, social media, digital communications and its website. We focus on delivering professional proactive, clear and strategic communications services, that support the Agency’s activities and promote ECHA’s work and achievements.

We support the delivery of ECHA’s mandate, purpose, vision and goals through:

• building, maintaining and protecting ECHA’s reputation by enhancing its visibility and stakeholder engagement;

• promoting chemical safety through science, collaboration and knowledge;

• positioning ECHA as the EU’s chemicals agency;

• ensuring that relevant, reliable and objective information is available for the public and interested parties; and

• optimising communications channels for effective outreach.

Job description:

The Seconded National Expert will work in the Communications Unit – G3.

The Communications Officer will contribute to the Unit’s daily interaction with internal and external stakeholders. The jobholder will also be responsible for relations with internal business areas on specific regulatory topics in support of ECHA’s external communications strategy. The role for this profile will be assigned according to the Unit’s needs and the jobholders’ competencies.

Duties will include, depending on needs:

External Communications:

• Drafting press releases, briefings, speeches etc.;

• Developing content for ECHA’s website;

• Dealing with press queries, interviews and briefings;

• Supporting senior management with media appearances;

• Organising and supporting events for external stakeholders;

• Support the production of webinars and videos;

• Support the management of the Agency's corporate communication channels and social media presence;

• Acting as a spokesperson when required; and

• Working with colleagues across ECHA to determine communication priorities and key messages to be delivered to internal and external stakeholders.

Internal Communications:

• Cooperating with colleagues in determining communications priorities;

• Content development for ECHA’s Intranet;

• Organising and supporting internal staff events; and

• General support to internal communication initiatives.

The Unit is responsible for a number of ECHA wide projects, where input may be required, including:

• Building a new website;

• Implementing the new ECHA corporate identity;

• ECHA’s 2027 Conference – 20-21 May 2027;

• ECHA’s 20th Anniversary 1 June 2027-31 May 2028;

• Chairing the EU Agencies Heads of Communications & Information Network – 1 March 2027 28 February 2028;

Requirements:

Successful completion of a full course of university studies attested by a degree, where the normal duration of university education is three (3) years or more.

Of your total professional experience, at least one (1) year must be in a field or fields relevant to the areas of work mentioned above e.g. for example, external/internal communications or stakeholder relations.

Only qualifications issued by EU Member State authorities or EEA authorities and qualifications recognised as equivalent by the relevant EU or EEA Member State authorities will be accepted.

Selection criteria: If you meet the requirements set out above, you will be assessed on the basis of the following selection criteria.

The candidates who are judged to be the most suitable on the basis of the selection criteria will be invited to a (remote) interview. The following will be considered as assets:

• Ability to communicate effectively in English at all levels both orally and in writing;

• Experience of working in a communications/stakeholder relations function in a complex regulatory environment; and

• Demonstrated understanding of the link between your current experience, the Communications Officer’s role and ECHA’s strategic priorities.

How to apply?

In order to be considered, applications must:

• Be submitted online, through the Apply button

• Include the following mandatory documents:

- CV in European Format: saved with CV_selection title_your surname and first name http://echa.europa.eu/documents/10162/17100/europass_cv_en.doc

- Employer Statement: saved with Employer statement_selection title_your surname and first name http://echa.europa.eu/documents/10162/17100/sne_employer_statement_en.pdf

- Letter of Motivation: saved with Motivation letter_selection title_your surname and first name

Candidates are requested to submit one application per profile. Candidates applying for several profiles should submit a separate application for each profile. Applications for each profile will be considered and assessed separately.

After successfully submitting your application, a confirmation message will appear on your screen and you will receive an automatically generated email as an acknowledgement of receipt, sent to the email address that you provided in the form.

Please contact us at traineeshipsecha [dot] europa [dot] eu (traineeships[at]echa[dot]europa[dot]eu) if you are not able to successfully submit your application.

NB: Applications that are incomplete or do not fulfil the criteria set out above will not be taken into account.

Assessment of application

Applicants will be assessed on the basis of their academic and professional qualifications and their relevance to the job. Short-listed candidates will be required to undergo a telephone and/or face-to-face interview. Human Resources will contact the successful candidates and their employers to initiate an exchange of letters between the Agency and the employers.

Protection of personal data

The information submitted during the selection process will be used solely for that purpose. The legal basis for the processing is found in the Rules on the secondment of national experts to the European Chemicals Agency (Executive Director Decision ED-0050). The European Chemicals Agency will ensure on its part that applicants' personal data is processed as required by Regulation (EC) No 45/2001 on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data by the Community institutions and bodies and on the free movement of such data. Only ECHA staff directly involved in the selection procedure in question shall have access to this data. For non-recruited candidates the personal data will be stored for a maximum period of two years. Documents related to recruited candidates are kept in the SNE’s personal file, which are kept until 10 years after the SNE has terminated the secondment at the Agency, provided there are no pending claims or any other open issues. Any party submitting personal data to ECHA is entitled to access and rectify that data (after the closing date of the application deadline, rectification is limited to identification data however). To exercise these rights, contact the data controller at traineeshipsecha [dot] europa [dot] eu (traineeships[at]echa[dot]europa[dot]eu) . Furthermore, you also have the right to recourse at any time to the European Data Protection Supervisor.

This selection procedure is intended to establish a reserve list of successful candidates. It is envisaged to start using the reserve list in Q4 of 2026/Q1 of 2027.

The Europol Recruitment Guidelines may be consulted for further details.

1. Organisational context

Organisational setting:
The post of Specialist - Specialist – Forensic Examiner (Decryption) is located is located in the Forensics Team in the Digital Support Unit, European Cybercrime Centre (EC3), Operations Directorate.

The Operations Directorate deals with the core business of Europol, improving the effectiveness and cooperation of the competent authorities in the Member States (MS) in preventing and combating serious and organised crime, as well as terrorism affecting the MS. This requires close cooperation with the Liaison Bureaux at Europol and via them with the Operational Teams in the MS.

Europol delivers a number of products and services to national law enforcement agencies to support them in their fight against international serious and organised crime, as well as terrorism.

The Operations Directorate hosts six distinct Departments: Operational and Analysis Centre (OAC), European Serious Organised Crime Centre (ESOCC), European Cyber Crime Centre (EC3), European Counter Terrorism Centre, European Financial and Economic Crime Centre (EFECC) and European Centre Against Migrant Smuggling (ECAMS).

EC3 serves as the centre for the MS fight against cybercrime in the European Union (EU), delivering operational and investigative support on complex cybercrime investigations. EC3 also provides support to the EU institutions and MS in building operational and analytical capacity for investigations and cooperation with external partners. EC3 is the collective voice of European cybercrime investigators across law enforcement and the knowledge hub of law enforcement on how to tackle cybercrime.

The Digital Support Unit is assisting EC3 Operations and provides horizontal support to other Operations Centres of Europol by delivering intelligence products, technical and forensic support, decryption and cryptocurrency tracing services and facilitating technical assistance in handling large datasets and conducting forensic examination through three dedicated teams: Cyber Intelligence Team (CIT), Forensics Team (FT) and Cryptocurrency Team.

Purpose of the post:
The jobholder is responsible for decryption services, digital forensics and advanced programming in order to support Europol and its partners in the fight against cyber-dependant crime.

Reporting lines:
The incumbent reports to the Head of Team Forensics/Head of Unit – Digital Support.

Job environment:
This post might require participation in a shift system including weekends and nights as well as on-call duty.

2. Functions and duties

The incumbent carries out the following main functions and duties:

- Provide expert decryption and digital forensic services in the field of competence of Europol’s EC3 DSU Forensics Team, including on-site assistance when required;
- Operate Europol’s Decryption Platform, liaise with Europol ICT and DG JRC to ensure continuity of Decryption Platform operations;
- Act as a liaison with EU MS, EU bodies, third countries, and international organisations on decryption and digital forensic matters;
- Support the projects of the Unit, such as organising meetings, training sessions and conferences;
- Represent Europol at high-level digital forensic and digital security events across Europe and internationally;
- Perform a technology foresight in the areas of decryption and digital forensics;
- Contribute to the development of new decryption, access to data and digital forensic methods, tools, and best practices;
- Independently draft and finalise reports, briefings, and strategic documents;
- Perform any other duties in the area of competence as assigned by the line management.

3. Requirements - Eligibility criteria

a. Candidates must

- Be a national of one of the Member States of the European Union and enjoy full rights as a citizen;
- Have fulfilled any obligations imposed by the applicable laws on military service;
- Produce appropriate character references as to his or her suitability for the performance of the duties;
- Be physically fit to perform the duties pertaining to the post as further specified in Article 13 of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (CEOS);
- Produce evidence of a thorough knowledge of one of the languages of the Union and a satisfactory knowledge of another language of the Union to the extent necessary for the performance of the duties.

b. Candidates must have

- A level of education which corresponds to completed university studies of at least three years attested by a diploma;

OR

- Professional training of an equivalent level in a relevant area (e.g.Police Officer’s School) and after having completed the training, at least the number of years of relevant professional experience as indicated below:

Duration of professional training Additional professional experience required for equivalency
More than 6 months and up to 1 year 3 years
More than 1 year and up to 2 years 2 years
More than 2 years 1 year

- In addition to the above at least 3 years of total professional work experience gained after the award of the diploma.

4. Requirements - Selection criteria

Selection criteria:
a. Professional experience:

Essential:

- Experience in digital forensics and decryption;
- Experience in designing, maintaining and operating large scale GPU based clusters;
- Experience in development, deployment and use of workload distribution/parallel computing solutions;
- Experience in programming using Python (CUDA, OpenCL would be an advantage);
- Experience in development and use of automation solutions for digital forensics and wordlist building techniques.

Desirable:

- Experience in development of decryption software (plugins for hashcat, JtR);
- Experience in Natural Language Processing (wordlist building) techniques;
- Experience in engaging with subject matter expert groups, management of such groups and networking.

b. Professional knowledge:
Essential:

- Knowledge of baseline digital forensic investigation and examination techniques;
- Knowledge of applied cryptography fundamentals - encryption algorithms, key derivation functions etc.;
- In depth knowledge of hashcat usage and it's modes of operation;
- Intermediate programming skills in Python.

Desirable:

- Knowledge of Natural Language Processing (wordlist building) techniques.

c. General competencies
Essential:
Communicating:

- Very good communication skills in English, both orally and in writing;
- Ability to draft clear and concise documents on complex matters for various audiences.

Analysing & problem solving:

- Keen eye for detail with the ability to maintain standards of accuracy under pressure of tight deadlines;
- Excellent analytical and critical thinking skills;
- Competent user of Microsoft Office applications (MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook) and the internet.

Delivering quality and results:

- High degree of commitment and flexibility;
- High level of customer and service-orientation.

Prioritising and organising:

- Good administrative and organisational skills;
- Very good interpersonal skills, with the ability to work well, both independently and in a team;

Resilience:

- Ability to remain effective under a heavy workload and demonstrate resistance to stress;
- Ability to handle exposure to disturbing child sexual abuse content while maintaining professional judgement and personal wellbeing.

Living diversity:

- Ability to work effectively in an international and multi-cultural environment.

d. Additional conditions:
Fulfil the condition stipulated in Article 5 of the Decision of the Executive Director on the Duration of contracts of employment for Temporary Agents, on the start date of the possible contract of employment which may be offered.

All applications for Temporary Agent posts must be submitted through the online recruitment system accessible via Europol’s website. For further information, please consult the Europol Recruitment Guidelines.

The Authority Authorised to Conclude Contracts of Employment (AACC) sets up a Selection Committee, composed of at least three members, consisting of one chair and at least one member from the administration and one member designated by the Staff Committee.

For restricted posts (including restricted - Annex II posts), the AACC designates up to two additional members of the Selection Committee if so requested by the Chairperson of the Management Board. Before the start of the selection procedure, the Selection Committee will decide which selection criteria will be used at each stage of the selection procedure. In case of candidates shortlisted for restricted posts (including restricted - Annex II posts), who had indicated membership of a competent authority in one of the Member States, Europol will seek confirmation from the relevant Europol National Unit to ensure that those candidates indeed belong to a competent authority.

1. Organisational context

Organisational setting:
The post of Specialist - Forensic Examiner (Digital Forensics) is located is located in the Forensics Team in the Digital Support Unit, European Cybercrime Centre (EC3), Operations Directorate.

The Operations Directorate deals with the core business of Europol, improving the effectiveness and cooperation of the competent authorities in the Member States (MS) in preventing and combating serious and organised crime, as well as terrorism affecting the MS. This requires close cooperation with the Liaison Bureaux at Europol and via them with the Operational Teams in the MS.

Europol delivers a number of products and services to national law enforcement agencies to support them in their fight against international serious and organised crime, as well as terrorism.

The Operations Directorate hosts six distinct Departments: Operational and Analysis Centre (OAC), European Serious Organised Crime Centre (ESOCC), European Cyber Crime Centre(EC3), European Counter Terrorism Centre, European Financial and Economic Crime Centre (EFECC) and European Centre Against Migrant Smuggling (ECAMS).

EC3 serves as the centre for the MS fight against cybercrime in the European Union (EU), delivering operational and investigative support on complex cybercrime investigations. EC3 also provides support to the EU institutions and MS in building operational and analytical capacity for investigations and cooperation with external partners. EC3 is the collective voice of European cybercrime investigators across law enforcement and the knowledge hub of law enforcement on how to tackle cybercrime.

The Digital Support Unit is assisting EC3 Operations and provides horizontal support to other Operations Centres of Europol by delivering intelligence products, technical and forensic support, decryption and cryptocurrency tracing services and facilitating technical assistance in handling large datasets and conducting forensic examination through three dedicated teams: Cyber Intelligence Team (CIT), Forensics Team (FT) and Cryptocurrency Team.

Purpose of the post:
The jobholder is responsible for providing digital forensics services and advanced programming in order to support Europol and its partners in the fight against cyber-dependant crime.

Reporting lines:
The incumbent reports to the Head of Team Forensics/Head of Unit – Digital Support.

Job environment:
This post might require participation in a shift system including weekends and nights as well as on-call duty.

2. Functions and duties

The incumbent carries out the following main functions and duties:

- Provide expert digital forensic services in the field of competence of Europol’s EC3 DSU Forensics Team, including on-site assistance when required;
- Operate, maintain and develop solutions designed to automate digital forensic and data minimisation workflows and reporting. Liaise with Europol ICT on this topic;
- Represent Forensic Team in EU MS, EU bodies, third countries, and international organisations on digital forensic matters;
- Support projects of the Unit, such as organising meetings, training sessions and conferences;
- Represent Europol at high-level digital forensic and digital security events across Europe and internationally;
- Contribute to and conduct research and development of new digital forensic and automation methods, tools, and best practices;
- Independently draft and finalise reports, briefings, and strategic documents;
- Perform any other duties in the area of competence as assigned by the line management.

3. Requirements - Eligibility criteria

a. Candidates must

- Be a national of one of the Member States of the European Union and enjoy full rights as a citizen;
- Have fulfilled any obligations imposed by the applicable laws on military service;
- Produce appropriate character references as to his or her suitability for the performance of the duties;
- Be physically fit to perform the duties pertaining to the post as further specified in Article 13 of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (CEOS);
- Produce evidence of a thorough knowledge of one of the languages of the Union and a satisfactory knowledge of another language of the Union to the extent necessary for the performance of the duties.

b. Candidates must have

- A level of education which corresponds to completed university studies of at least three years attested by a diploma;

OR

- Professional training of an equivalent level in a relevant area (e.g.Police Officer’s School) and after having completed the training, at least the number of years of relevant professional experience as indicated below

Duration of professional training Additional professional experience required for equivalency
More than 6 months and up to 1 year 3 years
More than 1 year and up to 2 years 2 years
More than 2 years 1 year

- In addition to the above at least 3 years of total professional work experience gained after the award of the diploma.

4. Requirements - Selection criteria

Selection criteria:
a. Professional experience:
Essential

- Preferably at least 5 years’ experience in digital forensics using standard forensic tools (commercial and open-source solutions);
- Experience in automating the processing and indexing of large structured and unstructured datasets;
- Experience in designing, building, and operating automated processing pipelines or workflow orchestration;
- Experience in software development in Python with proficiency in PowerShell, Bash and command-line scripting;
- Experience working with SQL and structured data stores, including SQLite;
- Experience with containerisation (Docker) and CI/CD, and with developing reusable APIs, libraries, plugins or automation frameworks.

Desirable:

- Experience integrating multiple third-party tools and services into end-to-end automated workflows via REST APIs, command-line interfaces and JSON/XML;
- Experience applying AI technologies to support digital forensic workflows;
- Experience integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into automation solutions.

b. Professional knowledge:
Essential:

- Knowledge in digital forensics investigation and examination techniques, including acquisition methods, file systems, data minimisation and chain of custody;
- Knowledge in Windows and Linux operating systems and their forensic artefacts;
- Knowledge of software engineering principles, including testing, debugging, and version control;
- Ability to analyse existing forensic processes, identify opportunities for automation, and engineer scalable, maintainable, and validated workflow solutions;
- Knowledge of Indexing and search at scale: text extraction, OCR, deduplication, index integrity, and the behaviour of Lucene/Elasticsearch/dtSearch-style engines.

Desirable:

- Applying AI and LLM’s within automation solutions, including their limitations, explainability and validation requirements in an evidential context.

c. General competencies
Essential:
Communicating:

- Very good communication skills in English, both orally and in writing;
- Ability to draft clear and concise documents on complex matters for various audiences.

Analysing & problem solving:

- Keen eye for detail with the ability to maintain standards of accuracy under pressure of tight deadlines;
- Excellent analytical and critical thinking skills;
- Competent user of Microsoft Office applications (MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook) and the internet.

Delivering quality and results:

- High degree of commitment and flexibility;
- High level of customer and service-orientation.

Prioritising and organising:

- Good administrative and organisational skills;
- Very good interpersonal skills, with the ability to work well, both independently and in a team;

Resilience:

- Ability to remain effective under a heavy workload and demonstrate resistance to stress;
- Ability to handle exposure to disturbing child sexual abuse content while maintaining professional judgement and personal wellbeing.

Living diversity:

- Ability to work effectively in an international and multi-cultural environment.

d. Additional conditions:
Fulfil the condition stipulated in Article 5 of the Decision of the Executive Director on the Duration of contracts of employment for Temporary Agents, on the start date of the possible contract of employment which may be offered.

5. Selection procedure

All applications for Temporary Agent posts must be submitted through the online recruitment system accessible via Europol’s website. For further information, please consult the Europol Recruitment Guidelines.

The Authority Authorised to Conclude Contracts of Employment (AACC) sets up a Selection Committee, composed of at least three members, consisting of one chair and at least one member from the administration and one member designated by the Staff Committee.

For restricted posts (including restricted - Annex II posts), the AACC designates up to two additional members of the Selection Committee if so requested by the Chairperson of the Management Board. The additional members shall consist of a representative of the Presidency of the Council of the European Union or one representative of the Presidency and one representative of another Member State.

The selection criteria, set out in this Vacancy Notice, will be assessed by the Selection Committee throughout the different stages of the selection procedure. Before the start of the selection procedure, the Selection Committee will decide which selection criteria will be used at each stage of the selection procedure. Certain selection criteria will be assessed only for shortlisted candidates during a written test and/or a competency-based interview.

The Selection Committee will assess the applications received in order to make an initial selection of those candidates meeting all eligibility criteria and matching best the selection criteria (suitability).

In case of candidates shortlisted for restricted posts (including restricted - Annex II posts), who had indicated membership of a competent authority in one of the Member States, Europol will seek confirmation from the relevant Europol National Unit to ensure that those candidates indeed belong to a competent authority.

The minimum pass-mark for being shortlisted, i.e. invited to participate in a post-related selection procedure, consisting of a written test and a competency-based interview, is established as 60% of the total maximum score.

The Selection Committee will shortlist the 8 highest scoring candidates. All candidates having a score equal to the 8th highest scoring candidate will be invited to take part in the selection procedure. At shortlisting stage, the Selection Committee will establish the pass-mark for the selection procedure.

It is intended for the selection procedure to be conducted remotely. Should the Selection Committee consider it necessary to conduct the selection procedure on-site at Europol, either in part or in full, in the interest of the proceedings, and subject to budget availability, the candidates invited to participate in the selection procedure will be informed accordingly.

After the selection procedure has taken place, the Selection Committee will establish a list of successful candidates, i.e. those scoring above the pre-defined pass-mark, which is shared with the AACC, for establishment of a Reserve list. A Reserve list is valid for 24 months.

Candidates who participated in the interview will be informed of the outcome, i.e. whether they have been successful or not.

After the selection procedure has taken place, the Selection Committee will establish a list of successful candidates, i.e. those scoring above the pre-defined pass-mark, which is shared with the AACC, for establishment of a Reserve list. A Reserve list is valid for 24 months.

Candidates who participated in the interview will be informed of the outcome, i.e. whether they have been successful or not.

The Selection Committee’s work and deliberations are confidential. It is forbidden for candidates to make direct or indirect contact with the members of the Selection Committee or for anyone to do so on their behalf.

All enquiries related to a selection procedure should be addressed to the Europol HR Operational Support Team at the following email address: C2-12europol [dot] europa [dot] eu (C2-12[at]europol[dot]europa[dot]eu).

Detailed information on the selection procedure- including enquiries, measures of redress and their applicable deadlines is available in the Europol Recruitment Guidelines, which can be found on Europol’s website www.europol.europa.eu.

6. Compensation and benefits

Scale: AD6
The gross basic monthly salary is EUR 6,961.29 (step 1) or EUR 7,253.84 (step 2).

The step in grade is determined on the basis of professional experience gained after the education required for the post and in line with applicable implementing rules.

Staff pay EU tax at source but salaries are exempt from national taxes. Compulsory deductions are made for health insurance, pension and unemployment insurance.

Subject to the applicable conditions being met, as defined in the EU Staff Regulations (EUSR)/CEOS and further specified in the case law of the Court of Justice of the European Union, allowances such as expatriation allowance (16% of basic gross salary) or foreign residence allowance (4% of basic gross salary), household allowance, dependent child and / or education allowance may be granted.

Staff enjoy worldwide insurance coverage by the Joint Sickness Insurance Scheme (JSIS) and are insured against sickness, the risk of occupational disease and accident.

Europol offers flexible working arrangements, a comprehensive provision for annual leave as well as parental leave supporting a healthy work-life balance.

Indicative net salary sample calculation AD6/1:
a) Staff member (single) in receipt of expatriation allowance (16%): EUR 7240
b) Staff member with two dependent children in their custody in receipt of expatriation allowance (16%): EUR 9436

The above information is indicative and for information purposes only. It is merely meant to give an indication of the possible net salary in light of the currently applicable amounts of the related allowances and the level of taxation. It has no legal value and no rights can be derived from it.
The information is based on figures applicable as of July 2025.

7. Terms and conditions

Contract of employment
The successful candidate will be engaged in the type of post Administrator and function group AD, grade 6 pursuant to Article 2(f) CEOS and Annex I to the EUSR.
The initial contract will be concluded for a period of 5 years (full-time – 40 hours a week). The contract may be renewed only once, in principle, for a period of 5 years.
The overall duration of the contracts on restricted posts of Europol staff members will be taken into account if they are successful in the selection procedure.

Conditions of engagement
Before the employment contract is concluded by Europol, the successful candidate will have to:

- declare any conflict of interest;
- undergo a pre-employment medical examination to confirm that he/she is physically fit to perform the duties pertaining to the post or, alternatively, receive the confirmation from Europol that he/she fulfils the conditions laid down in the Decision of the Deputy Executive Director of the Capabilities Directorate on the pre-employment medical examination available on www.europol.europa.eu;
- in case of candidates for restricted posts (including restricted - Annex II posts) who had indicated membership of a competent authority in one of the Member States, provide confirmation of his/her membership of a competent authority in one of the Member States within the meaning of the Article 2(a) of the Europol Regulation.
The place of employment will be The Hague, The Netherlands.
For further information on terms and conditions, please consult the EUSR/CEOS available on Europol’s website www.europol.europa.eu

Probation period
Engagement for this post is subject to the successful completion of a probationary period of 9 months.

Europol reserves the right to terminate the contract of employment during or at the end of the probation period in accordance with Article 14 CEOS.

Security screening and certificate of good conduct
Candidates who have been recruited to a post at Europol are required to furnish a valid certificate of good conduct before the start of their employment. The certificate of good conduct must be provided to Europol prior to the signature of the employment contract. The certificate of good conduct must be issued by the relevant authorities of the country of nationality of the candidate and must not be older than three months at the time of submission to Europol. Europol reserves the right not to proceed with the signature of the contract based on the content of the certificate or if the candidate fails to provide the certificate to Europol.

The certificate of good conduct does not substitute a valid security clearance required for all Europol staff at the level indicated in the vacancy notice. Failure to obtain the requisite security clearance may be cause for termination of the employment contract.

Candidates who currently hold a valid security clearance at the level indicated in the vacancy notice or above do not need to obtain a certificate of good conduct or a new security clearance and must provide a copy of the current security clearance certificate to Europol prior to the signature of the employment contract. Europol shall verify and confirm the continued validity of the security clearance. In case Europol determines that the security clearance is not valid, the candidate will be required to provide a valid certificate of good conduct prior to the signature of the employment contract. Europol may at any time terminate the employment contract if the result of the security screening is not positive and the necessary clearance level is not granted or extended.

The requested level of security clearance for this post is: CONFIDENTIEL UE/EU CONFIDENTIAL.

8. Additional information

Equal opportunity
Europol is an equal opportunity employer. Europol accepts applications without distinction on grounds of gender, sexual orientation, national, ethnic or social origin, religion or beliefs, family situation, age, disability, or other non-merit factors. All employment decisions are based on business needs, job requirements and qualifications, experience and skills.

Europol lives diversity and provides an inclusive work environment to all. Europol strives to recruit, develop and retain a diverse and talented workforce through application of equal opportunity and impartiality.

Privacy Notice
Regulation (EU) 2018/1725 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2018 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data by the Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies and on the free movement of such data, and repealing Regulation (EC) No 45/2001 and Decision No 1247/2002/EC, applies to the processing of personal data carried out in the process of selection and recruitment of staff at Europol, following the application of this Regulation to all administrative personal data held by Europol in accordance with Article 27a of the Europol Regulation.

For additional information, please consult the applicable privacy notice available on Europol’s website, also inserted in the EUROPOL RECRUITMENT GUIDELINES.

Statutory obligations upon leaving the service
Pursuant to Article 16 of the EUSR, EU officials and, by analogy, temporary agents continue to be bound by the duty to behave with integrity and discretion as regards the acceptance of certain appointments or benefits after leaving the service. Those staff members intending to engage in an occupational activity within two years of leaving the service shall inform their institution, so that it may take an appropriate decision in that respect. In cases where the intended activity is related to the work carried out by the staff member during the last three years of service and could lead to a conflict with the legitimate interests of the institution, the decision to be taken may include forbidding the staff member from undertaking it or giving its approval subject to any conditions it thinks fit.

Main dates

Selection procedure: October-November 2026

Application process and selection procedure
For further details on the application process and the selection procedure, please consult our FAQs or refer to the EUROPOL RECRUITMENT GUIDELINES available on Europol’s website.

Vacancy notice – Job title: Open-Source Intelligence analyst
  Contract Agent FGIV
  EEAS Headquarters – Job No 336466
WE ARE
The European External Action Service (EEAS) is the European Union’s diplomatic
service. Since 2011, the EEAS carries out the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy
(CFSP) to promote peace, prosperity, security, and the interests of the EU across the
globe. It brings together European civil servants, diplomats from EU Member States,
national experts and local staff worldwide.
The EEAS supports the High Representative in the exercise of her mandate to steer
the Union’s CFSP, including the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP), to
represent the EU on issues relating to the CFSP and to chair the Foreign Affairs Council.
It also supports her as Vice-President of the Commission with regard to her
responsibilities within the Commission, including the coordination of other aspects of
the EU’s external action. The EEAS works in close cooperation with the EU Member
States, the General Secretariat of the Council, the services of the Commission and the
Secretariat General of the European Parliament.
The EEAS Headquarters are in Brussels. It is also responsible for the management of
the network of 145 Union Delegations and Offices worldwide. These Diplomatic
Representations play a vital role in representing the EU in the country where they are
based, in promoting the values and interests of the EU, and in building networks and
partnerships. They are responsible for all policy areas of the relationship between the
EU and the host country/organisation.
The EU Intelligence and Situation Centre (EU INTCEN) is the exclusive civilian
intelligence centre of the EU, providing in-depth analysis for decision makers in all EU
Institutions. As such, EU INTCEN is a directorate of the EEAS that is directly attached
to the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy and
Vice-President of the European Commission. It comprises an Intelligence Analysis
Division (INTCEN.1) and a Support/Open-Source Research Division (INTCEN.2).
EU INTCEN also offers its services to the various EU decision-making bodies in the
fields of the EU Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP), Common Security
Defence policy (CSDP) and Counter Terrorism, as well as to the Member States. Under
the Single Intelligence Analysis Capacity (SIAC) agreement, it works hand in hand
with its military counterpart, the EUMS INT, in order to deliver joint civilian and military
intelligence assessments.
The Support/Open-Sources Research Division supports the Intelligence Analysis
Division of EU INTCEN and EUMS Int by providing open-source intelligence from
monitoring, collecting and assessing Open-Source information, political and diplomatic
reporting, using advanced research and analytical tools and services. Doing so,
INTCEN 2 complements and broadens the material and analytical basis for the
Intelligence output of INTCEN and EUMS Int.
WE PROPOSE
The position of open-source intelligence analyst - contract agent FGIV as per Article
3b of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union
(hereafter, the “CEOS”).
The Open-Source Intelligence Analysist will collect, research, monitor and analyse
open-source information including from social media, as well as political and diplomatic
reporting. He/she will analyse open-sources and draft open-source intelligence reports

in order to provide input to intelligence-based reports. The Contract agent will support
the work of dedicated INTCEN and SIAC Task Forces. The contract agent will also be
requested to monitor the political, economic, military and/or humanitarian situation in
selected countries/regions. He/she will produce Open-Source information research in
support of customers within the Single Intelligence Analysis Capacity (SIAC) of the
EEAS.
The Contract Agent will be part of an INTCEN.2 team and will work in close association
with the Intelligence Analysts of INTCEN's Intelligence Analysis Division and EUMS Int.
division.
Subject to having passed the CAST exam1, the successful candidate will be offered a
contract agent position (Function group IV), as per Article 3b of the CEOS, on the basis
of a contract with an initial duration of one year. This contract may be successively
renewed up to a maximum duration of six years2, subject to the maximum duration
of engagement by the EEAS allowed under successive limited duration contracts of
different types3.
PLACE and DATE OF EMPLOYMENT
EEAS Headquarters, Brussels, Belgium
Post available: 15/01/2027
LEGAL BASIS FOR RECRUITMENT TO THIS POSITION
The vacancy is to be filled in accordance with the conditions stipulated under the CEOS,
in particular Article 82 thereof.
WE LOOK FOR
A dynamic, proactive and highly motivated colleague with very good research,
analytical, IT, and organisational skills and with a developed sense of service. He/she
will be entrusted with the following main tasks:
•  Research and collect Open-Source information using automatised open-source
  research
•  Analyse Open-Sources on global issues and/or geographical issues in order to
  provide input to INTCEN/SIAC reports
•  Prepare analysis reports on global and security threats and geographical issues in
  support of intelligence work of SIAC
•  Monitor and provide updates on specific global and geographical issues.
Eligibility criteria4
In addition to the conditions set out in Article 82 of the CEOS and in the Commission
Decision C(2017) 6760 final , which is applicable to the EEAS by virtue of the Decision
ADMIN(2018) 4 of the High Representative, candidates must:
•  have passed a valid EPSO CAST in FG IV, or be registered in the EPSO Permanent
  CAST for FG IV (https://eu-careers.europa.eu/en/contract-staff-selection-
  procedures-always-open-registration). In the latter case, while the registration will
  make the candidate eligible for the selection procedure, the recruitment of a
  candidate on this vacant post will be subject to his/her successfully passing the
  CAST exam;
•  have completed university studies of at least three years attested by a diploma;
•  have the capacity to work in the languages of the CFSP and external relations
  (English and French) necessary for the performance of their duties;

will be considered as strong assets.

As a matter of policy, applications by individuals who have dual nationality, of which

there could be a conflict of interest or security risks.
In this context, all candidates shall fill with their application a declaration of
potential conflict of interest (see attached).
MEDICAL CLEARANCE

EEAS.
PERSONNEL SECURITY CLEARANCE (hereafter, “PSC”)

EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES
The EEAS strives to be a dynamic, respectful and inclusive Service. We value the talent
and professional excellence of our staff, and are committed to building an organisation
where gender equality and the respect of diversity are core values, as set out in the
EEAS Mission Statement and the EEAS Agenda for Diversity and Inclusion. The EEAS
is committed to achieving gender balance within its workforce and strives to avoid any
form of discrimination during this selection procedure, as per Article 1(d) of the SR.
We actively welcome applications from all qualified candidates without any
discrimination based on any ground. We commit to recruit candidates with the highest
standard of ability, efficiency and integrity, carrying out a selection based on merits
required for the post and from the broadest possible geographical basis among the EU
Member States.
The EEAS is committed to working with people with disabilities in the terms of the SR.
If, by virtue of your medical condition or special needs, you require reasonable
accommodation for a part or the entirety of this selection process, please send us an
email to CONTRACTAGENTS-HQ@eeas.europa.eu. Your request will be treated in strict
confidence and no record will be kept. If a candidate with a disability is selected for a
vacant post, the EEAS is committed to providing reasonable accommodation in
accordance with Article 1(d)(4) of the SR.
All selected candidates are expected to adhere to the Principles of Professional
Behaviour of the EEAS, which outline the need for integrity, transparency, respect,
professionalism and accountability, and a zero tolerance approach to any form of
harassment.
APPLICATION AND SELECTION PROCEDURE7
Please send your CV and cover letter (with your EPSO CAST number), in English or
French, and the attached declaration of potential conflict of interest via email, with
reference to the Vacancy Number in the Subject field, to:
EEAS-EU-INTCEN-ADMINISTRATION@eeas.europa.eu
Deadline for sending application: 03/11/2026 at 12.00 noon (CET).
Candidates shall draft their CV using the Europass CV, which can be found at the
following internet address:
http://europass.cedefop.europa.eu/en/documents/curriculum-vitae.

by the AACC.
It is recalled that, if the interest of the service so requires, the selection procedure can
be terminated at any stage.
In the interest of the service, after identifying the candidate that best fits the
requirements of the post as set out in the vacancy notice, the AACC may also establish
a reserve list of candidates. These candidates shall be informed that the reserve list
shall remain valid for a period of one year from when it is established and that it may
be used to fill the same post or an equivalent post in the EEAS with the same job
profile.
If the successful candidate accepts the position, they will be expected to take up duties
on the post. Consequently, their applications to other vacant posts within the EEAS
will only be considered after two years on the post. Derogations may be granted in
the interest of the service.

appointing authority of any actual or potential conflict of interest. In such cases, the
Appointing Authority shall take this into account in a duly reasoned opinion. If necessary,
the Appointing Authority shall take measures referred to in Article 11a(2)”.

Article 11a(2) of the SR:
“Any official to whom it falls, in the performance of his duties, to deal with a matter referred
to above shall immediately inform the Appointing Authority. The Appointing Authority
shall take any appropriate measure, and may in particular relieve the official from
responsibility in this matter”.

These provisions apply to temporary agents and contract agents in accordance
with Articles 11 and 81 of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the
European Union (CEOS).

It is the candidates’ duty to inform through this form the EEAS of any actual or potential

of conflict of interests and, if applicable, whether they constitute an issue for the

postings.institution: Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU)
postings.description:
Spécialiste finances/marchés/contrôle interne
Informations essentielles
Lieu de travail :
Luxembourg
Grade :
AD/AST
Type de contrat :
Agent temporaire
La mission de la Cour
La Cour de justice de l'Union européenne (CJUE) est au cœur de la justice européenne. En tant qu'autorité juridictionnelle de l'Union, elle veille, en étroite collaboration avec les juridictions nationales des États membres, à l'interprétation et à l'application uniforme des traités et du droit de l'Union européenne. En tant qu'employeur, la CJUE recherche l'excellence et valorise le multilinguisme, l'inclusivité, la diversité et la collaboration.
Quelle sera votre équipe ?
La direction du Budget et des affaires financières a pour mission d’assurer, avec ses trois unités, un large portefeuille d’activités relatives aux domaines du budget, de la comptabilité, de la vérification financière (ex ante et ex post), du système intégré de gestion budgétaire et financière (SAP), des marchés publics, du suivi des projets ainsi que du contrôle interne.
Quelle sera votre contribution ?
Nous recherchons des personnes pouvant intégrer la direction, selon les besoins, dans ses différents domaines d’intervention. Les personnes recrutées pourront être appelées à contribuer en particulier aux tâches suivantes :
Dans le domaine du budget : préparation et suivi du budget de l’institution.
Dans le domaine de la comptabilité : gestion de la comptabilité et de la trésorerie.
Dans le domaine de la vérification : effectuation de vérifications ex ante et ex post.
Dans le domaine des marchés publics : préparation et suivi de l’organisation de procédures de passation de marchés.
Autres domaines : taches liées au système de gestion financière et budgétaire, au suivi des projets menés par les services de l'institution, au suivi du dispositif de contrôle interne de l’institution, etc.
Êtes-vous la personne que nous recherchons ?
Un(e) professionnel(le) qui remplit les conditions de base suivantes :
Être ressortissant d’un des États membres de l’Union européenne (l’UE)
AD : Études universitaires d'au moins 3 ans sanctionnées par un diplôme.
AST : Diplôme universitaire, ou diplôme secondaire ouvrant l'accès au postsecondaire avec au moins 3 ans d'expérience professionnelle pertinente.
Une connaissance approfondie d'une des langues officielles de l'UE et une connaissance satisfaisante d'une autre. Pour des raisons professionnelles, les langues utilisées dans le service étant le français et l’anglais, une bonne connaissance de l’une et une connaissance satisfaisante de l’autre est requise. Les échanges avec d’autres services de l’institution se déroulent en effet en français et en anglais. L’anglais est nécessaire pour les échanges interinstitutionnels.
Un(e) professionnel(le) qui remplit les conditions souhaitées suivantes :
Selon les cas, les qualifications suivantes peuvent constituer un atout :
Une formation dans un domaine pertinent pour l’activité de la direction.
Une expérience professionnelle dans un des domaines d’activité de la direction.
Des connaissances linguistiques supplémentaires.

postings.title: Statistical Assistant - International trade in goods statistics - data production (monthly detailed data; data production, validation and quality-control tools)
postings.description:
VACANCY NOTICE FOR
  TEMPORARY AGENT SELECTION
  Statistical Assistant - International trade in
  goods statistics - data production (monthly
Job title
  detailed data; data production, validation and
  quality-control tools)
Reference  ESTAT/COM/2026/2074
Application deadline  30.10.2026 - 12.00 (Brussels time)
Directorate-General (full name) EUROSTAT
Unit  ESTAT.G.3 (Trade in goods)
Place of assignment  Luxembourg
Grade range  AST1-AST3
Domain  Economics, finance and statistics
Contract type  Temporary Agent 2b

About us
Eurostat, one of the Directorates-General of the European Commission, is the
statistical office of the European Union. Eurostat’s mission is to provide high quality
statistics and data on Europe.
Eurostat co-ordinates statistical activities at Union level and more particularly inside
the Commission.
Unit ESTAT.G.3 is responsible for providing high quality statistical information on
Europe's international trade in goods (ITGS). The statistical data on intra-EU and
extra-EU trade in goods is used by a wide range of Commission services to develop,
implement and evaluate EU policies closely related with potential economic growth
and employment creation. The European Central Bank uses the statistical data (in
particular euro area data) produced by Unit G.3 for the conduct of their monetary
policy.
Unit G3 is organised in four teams, respectively in charge of:

  •  Data production, COMEXT and international cooperation with enlargement
  countries,
  •  Aggregated data production (including monthly news release), data analysis,
  quality monitoring and dissemination,
  •  Legislation, methodology and international cooperation with international
  organisations,
  •  Micro-data exchanges.
The project involves the provision of assistance as a statistical assistant / domain
manager in the team in charge of the production of international trade in goods
statistics data production and, COMEXT, and cooperating closely with the statistical
officer in charge of the unit’s production, validation and quality-control tools.
About the role
Unit ESTAT.G.3 is seeking to hire one administrative agent.
The main responsibilities of the position include:
  •  Carrying out, as member of the production team, the monthly statistical
  production process, processing detailed trade data from Member States,
  EFTA and enlargement countries and liaising with the statisticians at national
  level with a view to publish high quality statistical data in a timely manner.
  •  Contributing to the ongoing development and implementation of validation
  rules, performing intensive testing on corporate and unit-specific validation
  tools.
  •  Contributing to the design and implementation of quality measures and
  controls in close collaboration with the team supervising the overall quality of
  international trade in goods statistics.
  •  Updating and improving metadata associated with data dissemination to
  ensure users have clear, high-quality documentation.
  •  Preparing and presenting documents and reports for relevant meetings.
  •  Documenting the unit’s production, validation and quality-control tools and
  related processes, and contributing to their continued improvement, including
  the implementation of enhancements and their systematic testing based on
  defined test cases and non-regression checks.
In addition to these tasks, depending on her/his knowledge and skills, the successful
candidate may contribute to other tasks under the responsibility of the unit.
Qualifications, experience and skills
We look for a dynamic and well-organised colleague who is interested in working in
statistics, particularly in the field of international trade in goods statistics, as a
statistical assistant / domain manager.
The successful candidate should have the following competences and skills:

  •  strong sense of responsibility, service-mindedness, commitment and
  flexibility and attention to detail;
  •  thoroughness in work, the ability to work autonomously with a spirit of
  initiative, and the ability to work effectively as part of a team, even under time
  constraints;
  •  clear and efficient communication skills, with a good oral and written
  command of English;
  •  ability to analyse statistical data;
  •  ability to work effectively with existing production tools;
  •  ability to analyse existing statistical processes and tools, identify
  opportunities for technical and structural improvements;
  •  ability to understand statistical processing requirements and translate them
  into clear business requirements and technical specifications, and to carry
  them through to implementation and testing;
  •  ability to analyse, debug, modify and document existing programs, including
  code developed by others; and
  •  sound knowledge and working experience with Oracle databases, PL/SQL,
  VBA.
Experience / knowledge in the following areas would be an advantage:
  •  International trade in goods statistics;
  •  Processing and validation of statistical data and metadata;
  •  Development or maintenance of data validation tools, in particular with rule-
  based validation languages or engines;
  •  EDIT language;
  •  Python language, in particular for data processing and automation;
  •  Analysis and documentation of existing software, including reverse
  engineering;
  •  Software maintenance practices, such as version control and regression
  testing.

How to express your interest?

You should send your documents in a single pdf in the following order:
1. your CV  2. completed application form.
Please send these documents by the publication deadline to ESTAT-HR-
APPLICATIONS@ec.europa.eu indicating the selection reference
ESTAT/COM/2026/2074 in the subject.
No applications will be accepted after the publication deadline.
Eligibility
For eligibility please consult this page with all the information needed.

postings.title: Translator/Language Technology Coordinator
postings.description:
VACANCY NOTICE FOR
  TEMPORARY AGENT SELECTION
Job title  Translator/Language Technology Coordinator
Reference  DGT/COM/2026/1916
Application deadline  16.10.2026 - 12.00 (Brussels time)
Directorate-General (full name)  Directorate-General for Translation
Unit  Swedish-language unit 2 (DGT.B.1.SV.2)
Place of assignment  Luxembourg
Grade range  AD5 - AD7
Domain  Languages, Information Technology
Contract type  Temporary Agent 2b

About us (“We are”)

We are DGT.B.1.SV.2, based in Luxembourg, one of the two units of the Swedish
language community at the Directorate General for Translation (DGT). Our mission
is to provide the Commission with high-quality translations into Swedish from all EU
languages, but mainly from English. We translate texts for different requester DGs
and services, in a wide variety of subject areas such as agriculture, regional policy,
health and food safety, internal market and industry, education and culture,
employment and social affairs.

About the role (“We propose”)

We offer a challenging and stimulating job as a translator and language technology
coordinator in a stable and well-integrated unit with some 25 translators and
assistants. The documents to be translated are mainly of a legal, administrative,
political or technical nature. However, we also translate press material, web texts
and documents intended for the general public. As a translator, you have the
opportunity to acquire new skills in a rich linguistic environment and use advanced
IT tools supporting the translation process. In addition to translating, you will revise
texts translated by colleagues and evaluate outsourced translations. You may also
specialise in a specific subject domain, develop working methods, be involved in
quality assurance and terminology work or act as lead translator for specific
translation projects. As a language technology coordinator, you will help promote
and raise awareness of available language technology, translation tools and

applications, and AI tools applied to translation. Furthermore, you will contribute to
testing and deployment of translation tools and applications in DGT and provide first
level technical support and advice regarding the use of these tools and applications.
The job involves close cooperation with all colleagues in the unit as well as with
Brussels-based colleagues, DGT's Language Technology community and DGT's
Field Officers in Stockholm and Helsinki.

Qualifications, experience and skills (“We look for”)

We look for a dynamic, team-oriented and reliable colleague with an excellent
command of Swedish (mother tongue), very good knowledge of English and
knowledge of at least one other official language of the European Union. Very good
general IT skills and practical experience with IT applications are indispensable, as
well as very good knowledge of language technology and translation tools and
applications. An interest and willingness to develop further in this area is also
essential since our working environment is highly technical. Studies and/or
experience in the fields of finance, economics, science or law are an asset, as is
knowledge or experience in the requesting DGs’ subject areas. Since we are a small
team, versatility and an ability to cover a broad range of the unit's portfolios and text
types are seen as an advantage. The job requires very good communication skills
and an ability to work closely with colleagues in a team of translators and assistants,
since we often deal with shared projects, short deadlines and urgent requests.

How to express your interest?

You should send your documents in a single pdf in the following order:
1. your CV  2. Complete application form.
Please  send  these  documents  by  the  publication  deadline  to
Annika.NASLUND@ec.europa.eu  indicating  the  selection  reference
DGT/COM/2026/1916 in the subject.

No applications will be accepted after the publication deadline.

Eligibility
For eligibility, please consult this page with all the information needed.
